name: +1 Dragon Edge Axe
descriptionMarkdown:
*Melee Weapon, uncommon*

**Damage:** 1d6 slashing (or 1d8 slashing versatile) | **Properties:** Versatile | **Weight:** 3 lb | **Value:** 0.50 gp

---

This weapon is made from the harvested remains of a fallen dragon. With a properly reclaimed claw or tooth, the resource can be forged into a simple Piercing or Slashing weapon whose latent draconic powers can appear in battle.

The first time you hit a creature on each of your turns with an attack roll you had Advantage|XPHB on using this weapon, its draconic magic comes forth to deal an extra 1d6 damage of a type corresponding to the original dragon's breath weapon. Weapons made from the claws or teeth of dragons change in rarity and power depending on the original dragon's age.

Young dragons' bones aren't as powerful as older ones and create Uncommon weapons. Adult dragons can produce Rare weapons, and ancient dragons can create Very Rare weapons, each granting a bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls determined by the weapon's rarity.

---

This weapon is made from the harvested remains of a fallen dragon. With a properly reclaimed claw or tooth, the resource can be forged into a simple Piercing or Slashing weapon whose latent draconic powers can appear in battle.

The first time you hit a creature on each of your turns with an attack roll you had Advantage|XPHB on using this weapon, its draconic magic comes forth to deal an extra 1d6 damage of a type corresponding to the original dragon's breath weapon. Weapons made from the claws or teeth of dragons change in rarity and power depending on the original dragon's age.

Young dragons' bones aren't as powerful as older ones and create Uncommon weapons. Adult dragons can produce Rare weapons, and ancient dragons can create Very Rare weapons, each granting a bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls determined by the weapon's rarity.

This weapon is made from the harvested remains of a fallen dragon. With a properly reclaimed claw or tooth, the resource can be forged into a simple Piercing or Slashing weapon whose latent draconic powers can appear in battle.

The first time you hit a creature on each of your turns with an attack roll you had Advantage|XPHB on using this weapon, its draconic magic comes forth to deal an extra 1d6 damage of a type corresponding to the original dragon's breath weapon. Weapons made from the claws or teeth of dragons change in rarity and power depending on the original dragon's age.

Young dragons' bones aren't as powerful as older ones and create Uncommon weapons. Adult dragons can produce Rare weapons, and ancient dragons can create Very Rare weapons, each granting a bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls determined by the weapon's rarity.

**Upkeep.** When you make an attack roll with a silver weapon or piece of ammunition, it takes a cumulative -1 penalty to attack rolls. The weapon or piece of ammunition is destroyed if the penalty reaches -5. The penalty can be removed by casting the Mending spell on the object or by succeeding on a DC 10 Dexterity check using Smith's Tools as part of a Short Rest|XPHB or Long Rest|XPHB.

name: Abjurer's Gilder
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon (by a Wizard)*

---

This golden badge is usually given to Wizards who either excel at or have mastered Abjuration magic as a symbol of their accomplishments. While wearing this badge, you always have the Shield spell prepared if it's in your spellbook, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can have prepared. In addition, when you are hit by an attack roll or targeted by the Magic Missile spell, you can take a special Reaction|XPHB, instead of your normal one, to cast Shield. This special Reaction|XPHB can be used before or after your normal Reaction|XPHB for the round, but it can't be used on the same turn as your normal Reaction|XPHB. Once you take this special Reaction|XPHB you can't do so again until the start of your next turn.

name: Aegis of Radiance
descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, rare (by a Cleric)*

**Armor Class:** 2 | **Weight:** 6 lb

---

This Shield emits a faint, holy glow when wielded and recognizes your devotion to a higher power. When you attune to the Shield, the emblem adorning its face changes to one that represents your chosen deity, allowing you to use the Shield as a Holy Symbol. You gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class|XPHB while holding this Shield, in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC.

While holding the Shield, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB and use a command word to cause it to magically shatter into countless fragments of pure light. The pieces of light protect you as if you were wielding the Shield, leaving your hands free. The light surrounds you for 1 minute, until you dismiss the effect as a Bonus Action|XPHB, or until you have the Unconscious condition or die, at which point the Shield rematerializes on the ground at your feet or strapped to your arm if you have a hand free. If your Holy Symbol is emblazoned upon or attached to the Shield, it floats prominently amidst the shards of light and continues to function as a Spellcasting Focus|XPHB for you. Undead creatures have Disadvantage|XPHB on attack rolls made against you while you're surrounded by the light in this way. The surrounding shards of light shed Bright Light|XPHB in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional 20 feet. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Amulet of Equilibrium
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon (Requires Attunement)*

---

This spiraling pendant is made of three magic-sensitive panes of colorful crystal. Each piece of crystal is attuned to a different arcane element. If you can cast spells, you can use the amulet as a Spellcasting Focus|XPHB while you're attuned to it.

The amulet has 4 charges and regains 2 expended charges daily at dawn. When you deal Cold, Fire, or Lightning damage to only one creature while wearing the amulet, you can expend any number of charges to reroll the same number of damage dice. You must use the new rolls.

Whenever you take Cold, Fire, or Lightning damage from an enemy, the amulet regains 1 expended charge.

name: Arcane Mirror
descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, very rare (Requires Attunement)*

**Armor Class:** 2 | **Weight:** 6 lb

---

This mirror-like Shield is enchanted with Abjuration magic that can reflect spells back at their source. While holding the Shield, you can take a Reaction|XPHB when you're hit by an attack to cast the Shield spell from it. You can't use this property again until you finish a Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB.

The Shield has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. When you succeed on a saving throw against a spell that targets only you or a spell attack roll misses you, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to learn the level of the triggering spell. As part of this Reaction|XPHB, you can expend a number of the Shield's charges equal to the spell's level to reflect that spell back at its source; you can't reflect a spell of level 7 or higher in this way. When you do, the caster of the spell must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the caster takes 1d8 Radiant damage for each charge you expended as a bolt of reflected arcane energy hits it. On a successful save, the caster takes half as much damage. If you reflect a spell in this way that would cause you to take half damage on a successful save, you take no damage instead.

reqAttune: by a Creature with an Intelligence of 17+
descriptionMarkdown:

**Damage:** 1d6 bludgeoning (or 1d8 bludgeoning versatile) | **Properties:** Versatile | **Weight:** 4 lb

---

When you attune to this Quarterstaff, it remains solid in your grip but feels pliable within your mind. Whenever you make an attack with this magic weapon, you can choose to make the attack at range. When you do, you use your mind to telekinetically curve the Quarterstaff into the form of a Longbow. While using it in this form, you're proficient with the Longbow and it doesn't have the H|XPHB|Heavy property. The bow is strung with an arcane energy that arcs between the rings on either end of the weapon. A glowing, magical arrow forms whenever the arcing energy is drawn back and fired. After the arrow hits or misses its target, it disappears and the Longbow reverts to its Quarterstaff form. This Longbow can only use the ammunition that it generates.

You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity for those rolls.

In addition, this Quarterstaff has 8 charges and regains 1d6 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. Immediately after you make an attack roll with this weapon as part of the Attack action, you can expend 1 charge to cast the Magic Missile spell from it as a Bonus Action|XPHB. When you do, the darts are fired from either the Longbow or the Quarterstaff's embossed faces.

name: Astral Bracelet
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, very rare*

---

Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

- Astral Bracelet of Energy
- Astral Bracelet of Heavens
- Astral Bracelet of Hells
- Astral Bracelet of Knowledge
- Astral Bracelet of Omniscience
- Astral Bracelet of Planebending

An Astral Bracelet is a powerful magical bangle that allows its wearer to see, commune, or otherwise manifest things using powers beyond the Material Plane. The metal and glyphs of each bracelet are related to the kind of power that it holds. You can pull the bracelet off and hold it in the palm of your hand as a Magic action. When you do, the bracelet unfurls to reveal the four inner rings collapsed within it, transforming the bracelet into an astronomical sphere. While the bracelet is transformed in this way, its inner rings slowly spin on their own.

The bracelet has 10 charges, which are only usable in its sphere form. It regains 2d4 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend its last charge, the sphere's spinning rings magically fold up again into the wearable bracelet. You can fold the rings back into place early as a Magic action.

**Spells.** Each kind of Astral Bracelet has a different list of spells that can be cast from it. If a spell cast in this way normally requires a Material component with a cost of 100+ GP, that component is still required when casting the spell. While holding the bracelet in its sphere form, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the corresponding spells from it, as shown below, using your spellcasting ability modifier and spell save DC.

name: Astral Sea Piercer
descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, legendary (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d8 piercing (or 1d10 piercing versatile) | **Properties:** Versatile | **Weight:** 2 lb

---

This golden War Pick was forged in the depths of the Astral Plane and leaves a faint trail of extraplanar energy behind it when swung. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and targets hit by it take an extra 1d4 Force damage. In addition, while you're in the Astral Plane, you always know the direction to the nearest portal to another plane of existence.

**Portal.** This weapon has 4 charges and regains 1d3 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can expend 1 charge to slam the War Pick into any flat, solid surface at least 5 feet in each dimension. When you do, you magically create a small planar rift, which fades after 1 minute. If you expend another charge in this way while there's another such rift within 300 feet of you, the two rifts tear open to form a portal between them. The portal lasts until the end of your next turn or until you close it early (no action required). When the portal closes, the rifts fade. Medium and smaller creatures and objects can move or interact freely through the portal while it's open, carrying with them any momentum they had through to the other side.

Both rifts must be placed on the same plane of existence, and if you create a second rift more than 300 feet away from the first, the first one fades. Rifts can be entered from any direction to travel through the portal. When you enter a rift in this way, you reappear 5 feet in front of the other rift.

In addition, you can expend 1 of the War Pick's charges when you hit a Small or larger creature with it. When you do, that creature takes an extra 1d8 Force damage as a rift appears on its body. Rifts that appear on a creature in this way are attached to the creature and move with it until a portal is opened. When a portal opens between two rifts and at least one of the rifts is attached to a creature, the attached creature or creatures must succeed on a DC 17 Charisma saving throw or be immediately shunted through the portal to the other rift's location. Large and larger creatures automatically succeed on this saving throw.

name: Band of Mirrored Essence
descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, rare (Requires Attunement)*

---

This unassuming platinum ring is polished to a mirror finish. When you reduce a Small or larger enemy to 0 Hit Points|XPHB while wearing the ring, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to cause the ring to capture a portion of that creature's essence. Looking into the ring shows the reflection of the creature whose essence is held inside. Once you capture an essence with the ring, it can't do so again for 1d8 hours. The ring can only have one essence at a time. If you capture an essence when the ring already has one, you replace the original.

As a Magic action, you can release the captured essence and assume either the creature's appearance or one of its features, as detailed below.

**Assume Appearance.** The creature must be no more than one size larger or smaller than you for you to take on its appearance. When you do, you don't physically change in size or shape, but your body is shrouded in a convincing illusion. Your voice changes to match the creature's, and you can understand any of its known languages but can neither read nor speak any language that you don't already know. Another creature can see through the illusion by succeeding on a DC 16 Intelligence (Investigation) check.

Physical interaction with this illusory form reveals it to be an illusion, because things can pass through it. The illusion lasts for 8 hours. It ends early if you dismiss it as a Bonus Action|XPHB or if you have the Unconscious condition or die.

**Assume Feature.** If you assume one of the creature's features, your body or mind temporarily changes to accommodate the new ability. You can choose to gain one skill or saving throw proficiency, Damage|XPHB Resistance|XPHB, Condition|XPHB Immunity|XPHB, special sense, or language known that the creature had. If the creature could breathe underwater, you can choose to gain that feature instead. You retain this feature for 8 hours. You lose it early if you dismiss it as a Bonus Action|XPHB or if you have the Unconscious condition or die.

Another creature can see through the illusion by succeeding on a DC 16 Intelligence (Investigation) check.

Physical interaction with this illusory form reveals it to be an illusion, because things can pass through it. The illusion lasts for 8 hours. It ends early if you dismiss it as a Bonus Action|XPHB or if you have the Unconscious condition or die.

Assume Feature.

If you assume one of the creature's features, your body or mind temporarily changes to accommodate the new ability. You can choose to gain one skill or saving throw proficiency, Damage|XPHB Resistance|XPHB, Condition|XPHB Immunity|XPHB, special sense, or language known that the creature had. If the creature could breathe underwater, you can choose to gain that feature instead. You retain this feature for 8 hours. You lose it early if you dismiss it as a Bonus Action|XPHB or if you have the Unconscious condition or die.

The compasses spin wildly if the two bands are worn on different planes of existence.

name: Bard-in-a-Box
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, common*

---

This small music box can play songs upon request. While holding it, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to command the box to magically play a song for which it has music, causing the contraption to emit a slightly tinny rendition of the musical number. The box can know the music for up to five songs at a time but can't recreate lyrics or other creature sounds. The box has a knob on its side to adjust its volume, allowing it to be as quiet as a whisper or as loud as a scream.

Sheet music can be fed into the box through a narrow slot along the bottom of the device. Sheets must be labeled with a song title, page number, and instrument in order for the box to learn the music. Sheets failing to meet these requirements cause the box to make a sad, discordant noise before being spat back out. Once a sheet is successfully fed into the box, it is consumed and can't be retrieved.

If the box already knows five songs and a new sheet of music is successfully fed into it, it quickly plays several bars of the oldest song it knows before it slows to a stop and forgets the music.

name: Baton of Many Sizes
descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, uncommon*

---

While holding this segmented, 1-foot-long rod, you can take a Magic action and use a command word to cause it to extend in either direction. The rod can extend up to be up to 50 feet long or as far as the surrounding space allows. If the rod touches another creature or surface before reaching its full length, the rod stops moving in that direction. If it stops moving against a solid, unmoving surface, the rod fills the gaps to hold firm against it.

The rod is unwieldy to hold once it's longer than 10 feet, forcing you to make a Strength (Athletics) check at the start of each of your turns to maintain your hold of it while it's extended beyond that range. The DC for this check is equal to 8 plus 1 for every 5 feet beyond 10 that the rod is extended. For example, the DC is 9 while the rod is 15 feet long, but 16 while it's a full 50 feet. If you drop the rod or use it to make an attack while it's extended more than 10 feet, it immediately retracts back to its shortened length. You can also cause it to retract by taking a Magic action and repeating the command word.

In order to create this bond, you and an ally with whom you are close perform a brief, 1-minute ritual to connect your destinies and forge a blood pact. ---

This metal brooch features a rotatable dial and can be used to secure a cape or adorn a piece of clothing. While wearing the brooch, you can cast the Enlarge/Reduce spell on yourself by turning the dial toward either the larger or smaller figure adorning the sides of the brooch. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

While under the effects of this spell, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to overload the brooch by forcibly twisting the dial beyond its normal limits. When you do, your size magically changes by an additional category: you either grow a second size larger if you have the "enlarge" effect or shrink a second size smaller if you have the "reduce" effect. Your size can't be larger than Huge or smaller than Tiny by overloading the brooch, and your damage and weight are increased or decreased as if you were affected by a second instance of the Enlarge/Reduce spell.

When you return to your original size after overloading the brooch, you have the Incapacitated condition and a Speed|XPHB of 0 until the end of your next turn. Once the brooch has been overloaded, its properties can't be used again until 7 days have passed.

When you reduce a Large or smaller creature to 0 Hit Points|XPHB using this weapon, you can choose to encase that creature in ice. An affected target must succeed on a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw or take 2d8 Cold damage as a frozen spike erupts from the ground beneath it. In addition, when an ally within 15 feet of you rolls a 19 or 20 on the d20 for a Death Saving Throw|XPHB, it regains 1 Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point, and you can take a Reaction|XPHB and expend 1 charge to grant them 2d6 Temporary Hit Points|XPHB. name: Clockwork Faefly
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon*

---

This brass clockwork mechanism is 2 inches long and whirs with the hum of tiny gears inside. You can tap the head of the faefly twice as a Bonus Action|XPHB. When you do, it magically begins to flutter 5 feet in the air until a creature grasps it or it is reduced to 0 Hit Points|XPHB. The faefly has AC 10, HP 10, Immunity|XPHB to Poison and Psychic damage, and Resistance|XPHB to all other damage. If you move more than 60 away feet from the hovering faefly, it follows you until it is within 60 feet of you. It takes the shortest route to do so. If prevented from moving, the faefly sinks gently to the ground and becomes inactive, and its light fades out. While it's flying, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB and use a command word to cause it to move up to 20 feet.

If you are within 60 feet of the faefly, you can use another command word as a Magic action to cause it to emit light as if targeted by the Light spell or cast Faerie Fire (save DC 13), affecting a 20-foot Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube originating from the faefly. Faerie Fire doesn't require Concentration|XPHB when cast in this way, but it ends early if the faefly drops to 0 Hit Points|XPHB. Once the Faerie Fire spell is cast from the faefly, it can't be cast in this way again until the next dawn.

The faefly is a magical object, not a creature. If the Mending spell is cast on it while it has at least 1 Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point, it regains 2d6 Hit Points|XPHB. If the faefly drops to 0 Hit Points|XPHB, it can't be used again until 2 days have passed, at which point it regains all its Hit Points|XPHB.

This pill-shaped magical mechanism is 2 inches long and made of brass and glass. It has a pair of tiny wings that silently keep it aloft. It hovers up to 5 feet in the air and does its best to stay at your side within your space. The bee can pass through another creature's space and doesn't provoke Opportunity Attack.

The bee has 8 charges and regains 1d6 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. While the bee is within your space, you can use a command word as a Bonus Action|XPHB and expend up to 3 charges to send the bee to magically heal a creature you can see within 20 feet of you. The bee flies out and touches its stinger to the target, causing the target to regain 1d6 Hit Points|XPHB for each expended charge and emitting an instantaneous burst of Bright Light|XPHB that fills the target's space. The bee then returns to your space.

The bee is a magical object, not a creature. It has AC 15, HP 10, Immunity|XPHB to Poison and Psychic damage, and Resistance|XPHB to all other damage. If the bee drops to 0 Hit Points|XPHB, it can't be used again for 24 hours, at which point it regains all its Hit Points|XPHB.

name: Clockwork Inkbeetle
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon*

---

This minuscule, mechanical beetle is 1 inch long and quietly whirs with a mix of magical and mechanical forces. Placing the beetle on a piece of parchment you're holding or carrying causes it to spring to life and begin tracking your travels. As you move, so does the beetle, leaving behind a small line of ink. The ink immediately dries and doesn't dissolve in water. In addition, the beetle's small frame allows it to move even while enclosed in a book or similar enclosure without losing its sense of movement or direction.

The beetle mirrors your movement to create a to-scale map of your journey, drawing 1 inch of ink in your choice of the following scales: 20 feet per inch, 200 feet per inch, 2 miles per inch, or 20 miles per inch. You can rotate the dial on the beetle's underside to change the scale as a Magic action. The beetle is immune to magical effects that would otherwise alter its sense of direction.

The beetle always knows which way is magnetic north. When placed on a piece of parchment for the first time, it crouches down to stamp a small compass rose on the sheet before it begins to move. If the beetle runs out of space on the parchment to travel, it stops moving in that direction and emits a clicking sound that can be heard by creatures within 5 feet of it.

Attaching one Band of the Found and Lost to the beetle while you wear the other allows the beetle to move and trace your movements in this way from afar as long as you are both on the same plane of existence.

name: Companion's Band
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, common (Requires Attunement)*

---

This woven band can be worn as a necklace or bracelet by resizing its strap. While wearing the band, you can take a Magic action to summon a spectral companion that appears in a space you can see within 5 feet of you. The companion has the appearance of a dog, cat, bird, or similar Small or smaller Beast of your choice. Its form is translucent and immaterial but feels warm to the touch. It emits Dim Light|XPHB in a 5-foot radius. The companion remains until dismissed (no action required) or until you remove the band. It is a creation of magical force, not a creature; it doesn't occupy space and doesn't require air, food, or drink. It is Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly to you and other creatures you choose. It stays within 30 feet of you at all times and moves through objects as necessary in order to do so. If it's unable to reach you, it disappears until summoned again. The companion wears a spectral copy of the band on its neck or limb (your choice).

The companion understands the emotion and intent of your commands but can't speak or understand language. Attempting to read the companion's thoughts only reveals an overwhelming sense of love and affection for you.

Once the same spectral companion has remained or has been summoned at least once a day for 7 consecutive days, the band and companion become permanently linked to you. When this happens, the band no longer requires you to be attuned to it in order to use it, but no other creature can attune to it. Once the band is linked to you in this way, you can summon your linked companion as a Bonus Action|XPHB instead of a Magic action. In addition, the companion becomes partially physical, allowing you and creatures you choose to be able to gently pet and hold its otherwise spectral form.

If you die, the band can be attuned to by a different creature. The linked companion follows you to whatever afterlife awaits you or reappears if you're resurrected and summon it once again.

name: Container of Heat and Frost
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, common*

---

This heavy iron container is adorned with three arcane symbols along the edge of its removable lid. The container can hold up to 1 gallon of liquid. As a Magic action, you can press one of the container's arcane glyphs to heat the liquid inside to a boil (212 degrees Fahrenheit), chill it (33 degrees Fahrenheit), or maintain its current temperature (keeping it between 33 and 212 degrees Fahrenheit). Once pressed, the selected glyph glows either red, blue, or yellow, respectively.

It takes 1 minute to boil or chill a liquid. Pressing the glyph again as a Magic action ends the heating or cooling process early. After boiling or chilling the liquid, the container maintains its hot or cool temperature, respectively.

*Martial Weapon, rare (by a Creature of Good Alignment)*

**Damage:** 1d4 slashing | **Properties:** Finesse, Reach, Light | **Weight:** 3 lb

---

This slender Whip's grip is feathered and comfortable to wield. Its weight has been magically reduced and it gently sways on its own. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and it has the L|XPHB|Light property.

Once on each of your turns when you take the Attack action, you can forgo one of your attacks, instead using the Whip to attempt to bind a Medium or smaller creature within the Whip's reach. The target must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it has the Grappled condition and takes 1d4 Bludgeoning damage as it's constricted. If a target that's already Grappled by the Whip fails another save against you using the Whip in this way, it has the Restrained condition instead.

A target that is Grappled or Restrained by the Whip can use its action to make a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check, ending the condition on itself on a success. Moving more than 10 feet away from the target or dropping the Whip also ends the condition on the target. Until the condition ends, you can't use the Whip against a different target.

**Flight of the Couatls.** While you're attuned to three items with this property, you gain a Fly Speed|XPHB of 30 feet. If you already have a Fly Speed|XPHB, it increases by 30 feet instead.

On a failed save, the chosen limb is pinned by radiant tethers of magic, holding it to the target's body or an adjacent surface (if any) for up to 1 minute.

Depending on the pinned limb, the target may gain the Prone condition, be unable to move, or make attack rolls with Disadvantage|XPHB (GM's choice) while the limb remains pinned in this way. To escape, the target or a creature within 5 feet of it must take an action to make a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check, freeing the target on a success.

**Flight of the Couatls.** While you're attuned to three items with this property, you gain a Fly Speed|XPHB of 30 feet. If you already have a Fly Speed|XPHB, it increases by 30 feet instead.

name: Doodle Ring
descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, common*

---

This magic wooden ring is always covered in splotches of charcoal, ink, or paint, regardless of how well or often it's cleaned. While wearing the ring on a finger, you can touch that finger to a solid surface and begin to draw. The drawing uses your finger to make marks as if it were a piece of charcoal, an ink quill, or a paintbrush (your choice). The marks you make can be in any color. Any drawing made by the ring can be easily smudged or washed away without leaving any marks behind. The ring can have up to a total of 5 square feet covered with drawings in this way at any time. Drawing more than that begins to erase the previous marks, and any mark it makes is magically erased after 24 hours.

name: Doomsday Cookie
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon*

---

This black sugarpaste cookie is made using a grim recipe passed down through generations of Clerics devoted to gods of death. Inside this hollow cookie is a blank strip of enchanted paper whose writing only appears when you break open the cookie. The paper's writing vaguely predicts the manner in which you'll die. When you open this cookie, roll 1d20 and use the table below to determine the paper's prediction.

Once a creature's death has been predicted in this way, all future Doomsday Cookie papers will predict the same outcome for that creature. If a creature dies in a way foretold by the cookie (at the GM's discretion), the cookie's paper transforms into a Spell Scroll of Revivify. This scroll can only be used on the creature whose passing it foretold. If the scroll is unused within 1 minute, it crumbles into flour.

Regardless of its grim foretellings, the cookie itself is a delicious snack that is sweet, salty, and smoky.

| 2 | The light of the full moon casts the deepest shadows. |

| 5 | Betrayal strikes deeper than any blade. |
| 6 | Hasty hands make for quick lives. |

| 8 | Getting ahead of yourself may separate you both. |

| 17 | Stars die as new ones rise. |
| 18 | Cold. So cold. |
| 19 | The stench of failure burns your nostrils. |
| 20 | Rocks fall. You die. |

descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, legendary (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d10 piercing | **Properties:** Heavy, Reach, Two-Handed | **Weight:** 6 lb

---

This slender, iridescent Lance is covered in an enchanted finish that resembles the hardened scales of many dragons. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While attuned to the weapon, you know Draconic|XPHB.

This Lance has 8 charges and regains 1d4 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a target with the Lance, you can expend 1 charge to deal an extra 3d6 Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison damage (your choice) to the target. If you expend a charge in this way when you hit a Dragon, it must also succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition until the start of your next turn.

Whenever you expend a charge in this way, you can expend a second charge to deal an additional 1d6 damage of the same type to the target, and the target can't take Reaction|XPHB|Reactions until the start of its next turn.

**Wyrmling Steed.** In addition, while holding the Lance, you can cast the Find Steed spell from it. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn. When you cast the spell in this way, you can choose to summon a dragon wyrmling instead of a normal mount by expending a number of charges equal to its Challenge Rating|XPHB (maximum 2). You determine the kind of dragon summoned, but its alignment toward Good or Evil must be the same as your own; if your alignment is Neutral, you can summon a wyrmling of either alignment. The wyrmling counts as one size larger when used as a mount and can't use its breath weapons.

**Forceful Impact.** If you move at least 20 feet in a straight line toward a Medium or smaller target immediately before making a melee attack roll with the Lance while within 5 feet of the target, you make the attack roll with Advantage|XPHB. On a hit, you can immediately make an additional melee attack roll with the Lance as part of the initial attack. This additional attack roll must be made against a different target directly behind the first that is within 5 feet of it and isn't behind Cover|XPHB|Total Cover.

**Armor Class:** 2 | **Weight:** 6 lb

---

This Shield is made from a piece of reclaimed dragon turtle shell. The dragon turtle head sculpture adorning its front is made of brass, and it magically creates and heats a small reservoir of water that replenishes daily at dawn. When you take Fire damage while holding the Shield, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to use a command word. When you do, the water inside it is superheated, reducing the Fire damage you take by half. Once this property is used, the Shield's reservoir is empty and can't be used again in this way until the next dawn when it replenishes or until it's submerged in nonmagical salt water for 1 hour.

**Damage:** 1d8 slashing (or 1d10 slashing versatile) | **Properties:** Versatile | **Weight:** 3 lb

---

This magnificent blade is crafted from the remains of an ancient dragon. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The weapon deals an extra 2d6 damage on a hit if the target is a Dragon. In addition, while you're attuned to this weapon, you know Draconic|XPHB.

**Kindled Cleave.** When you're affected by a Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile dragon's breath weapon, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to hold the blade in front of you. When you do, the sword splits the breath weapon's area of effect, leaving you and any creature in a 30-foot Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone behind you unaffected by it. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

When you use this property to split a breath weapon that deals damage, the sword gives off an elemental haze corresponding to the dragon's breath weapon. The haze lasts for 1 minute, and it sheds Bright Light|XPHB in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional 10 feet. The first target you hit with an attack roll using the sword while it has this haze takes an extra 6d6 damage of the breath weapon's damage type. This extra damage ignores Resistance|XPHB and Immunity|XPHB.

**Lesser Draconic Resistance.** If you fail a saving throw by 4 or less, you can choose to succeed instead. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

The cape creates illusions of faraway places that are visible only to creatures that are at least 30 feet away from it. While wearing the mantle, creatures more than 30 feet away from you have Disadvantage|XPHB on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight to perceive you, and they make ranged attack rolls against you with Disadvantage|XPHB. This property is suppressed while you have the Incapacitated or Restrained condition or are otherwise unable to move.

In addition, you can cast the Dream spell (save DC 16) from the mantle over the course of 1 minute, using yourself as the messenger within the dream. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until 7 days have passed.

name: Dryadleaf
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, common*

---

This magic plant only grows at the base of trees that are often stepped through by dryads. Its leaves continuously shift as if by a breeze. Touching the plant, even gently, causes its leaves to stop their gentle swaying for 1 minute.

Dryadleaf plants only grow up to four leaves at a time and are found in the wild with 1d4 matured leaves. Leaves are fully matured once they have a thin yellow rim. You can take a Magic action to eat a mature Dryadleaf. When you do, you can speak to Beasts, Plant creatures, and nonmagical plants for 1 minute as if you shared a language. Once it's been picked, a Dryadleaf retains this property for 7 days before it wilts.

You can move the plant to a pot over the course of 1 minute. When you do, make a DC 15 Intelligence (Nature) or Wisdom (Survival) check. On a success, the delicate plant survives the transfer to a new pot. On a failure, the plant is irreversibly damaged and dies.

The plant can survive with surprisingly little air, allowing it to survive in an extradimensional space such as a Bag of Holding or Portable Hole. As long as it's watered lightly each day and given a moderate amount of sunlight (weather and environment permitting), the plant grows 1d4 missing mature leaves every 7 days.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon (Requires Attunement)*

---

This thick glove is ornamented with eagle feathers and fitted with an enchanted silk lining. You can use the glove to cast the Find Familiar spell as a Magic action instead of its normal casting time. When you do, the familiar takes the form of an Eagle. The familiar disappears if you are no longer attuned to the glove. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

**Summon Giant Eagle.** You can focus on the glove for 1 hour to magically summon a Giant Eagle that appears in an unoccupied space that you can see within 30 feet of you. It disappears when it drops to 0 Hit Points|XPHB, after 12 hours, or if you dismiss it (no action required). Once the creature disappears, it can't be summoned again until 2 days have passed.

The creature is an ally to you and your allies. In combat, the creature shares your Initiative|XPHB count, but it takes its turn immediaftely after yours. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don't issue any, it takes the Dodge action and uses its movement to avoid danger.

The creature has a carrying capacity of 480 pounds and can travel at a rate of 8 miles per hour while flying. It must rest 1 hour for every 3 hours it flies, and it can't fly for more than 9 hours each time it's summoned.

name: Edible Book of Recipes
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, very rare*

---

This tome of cooking recipes is enchanted to turn sheets of fine paper into delectable meals. You can write a simple recipe on one of the book's pages over the course of 1 minute. As you do, the paper becomes aromatic, smelling like the cuisine you're writing. The sheet of paper has the taste, texture, and smell of the food described on its page. Eating the sheet as a Magic action nourishes you as if you ate a meal.

If you add a more complex recipe to the book that takes at least 10 minutes to write—potentially using sensory language, descriptions of fine ingredients, or illustrations of the dish—eating the delicious sheet of paper provides enough nourishment to sustain a creature for one day. When a creature eats a sheet detailing one of these complex recipes, its Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum increases by 1d10 + its Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus, and it gains the same number of Hit Points|XPHB, until it finishes a Long Rest|XPHB. In addition, if the creature has the Poisoned condition or is affected by a magical contagion, it can immediately repeat the save to end it. A creature can only gain the benefits of a complex recipe once every 24 hours.

In addition, you can use this book as a Spellcasting Focus|XPHB when casting the Create Food and Water spell if you have it prepared or can otherwise cast it. When you do, the food and drink you create can be aromatic and flavorful, recreating recipes of your choice from the book.

The book can hold up to 50 pages. A book found as treasure usually has 3d10 + 10 blank pages as well as 1d10 filled pages containing complex recipes.

When you remove the last page from the book or attempt to rebind the book, roll 1d20. On a 1, the tome bursts into flame, destroying the book and leaving the air in a 60-foot radius smelling like wine and fine cooking. The smell remains in the area for 30 days. After 1 minute, the book's tattered remains transform into a bountiful meal, duplicating the effect of the Heroes' Feast spell. On any roll other than a 1, the book can be rebound using fine paper that costs at least 5 GP per page.

In addition, you can use this book as a Spellcasting Focus|XPHB when casting the Create Food and Water spell if you have it prepared or can otherwise cast it. When you do, the food and drink you create can be aromatic and flavorful, recreating recipes of your choice from the book.

The book can hold up to 50 pages. A book found as treasure usually has 3d10 + 10 blank pages as well as 1d10 filled pages containing complex recipes.

When you remove the last page from the book or attempt to rebind the book, roll 1d20. On a 1, the tome bursts into flame, destroying the book and leaving the air in a 60-foot radius smelling like wine and fine cooking. The smell remains in the area for 30 days. After 1 minute, the book's tattered remains transform into a bountiful meal, duplicating the effect of the Heroes' Feast spell. On any roll other than a 1, the book can be rebound using fine paper that costs at least 5 GP per page.

name: Eldritch Scarf
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, rare*

**Weight:** 1 lb

---

This dark scarf moves slowly on its own and is always wrinkled. The scarf hides an extradimensional space within its folds that can only be reached while its worn. The space can hold 60 pounds of material, not exceeding a volume of 6 cubic feet. The scarf always weighs 1 pound, regardless of its contents. When you place an object in this space (no action required), your hand vanishes into the scarf's loose folds.

You can't retrieve items placed within the scarf with your hands. Instead, retrieving an item requires you to take a Bonus Action|XPHB to mentally control the scarf while wearing it, causing its frayed, handlike ends to reach into the space and retrieve a stored item of your choice. The hands can carry up to 10 pounds, and they drop any object weighing more than that on the ground at your feet.

If the scarf is ironed or otherwise flattened, the items stored inside are squeezed out, spilling forth unharmed from the ends of the scarf. If the scarf is destroyed, its contents are lost forever, although an Artifact always turns up again somewhere. A living creature can't be placed inside the scarf.

In addition, while wearing the scarf, you can take a Magic action to mentally control it, using the scarf's frayed hands instead of your own to perform a simple task within 5 feet of you, such as to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial. The hands can't attack or activate magic items.

Placing the scarf inside an extradimensional space created by a Bag of Holding, Portable Hole, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within 10 feet of the gate and not behind Cover|XPHB|Total Cover is sucked through it and deposited in a random location on the Astral Plane. The gate then closes. The gate is one-way only and can't be reopened.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, rare*

---

This ring's tiny chains rotate slowly around your finger while worn. Whenever you are affected by a spell that restores Hit Points|XPHB, such as Cure Wounds or Healing|XPHB Word, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to repeat the saving throw against an Enchantment spell that's currently affecting you.

Once this property is used, it can't be used again until 1d4 days have passed.

name: Essence of Rage
descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, rare*

---

This swirling potion tastes like iron and bitter raisins. When you drink this potion, you enter a rage that lasts for 1 minute or until you have the Incapacitated condition. This rage grants you the same effects as the level 1 Barbarian class feature with the following changes:

- You can enter and maintain this rage even if you're wearing Heavy armor.
- If you end your turn and haven't made an attack roll against an enemy, forced an enemy to make a saving throw, or taken a Bonus Action|XPHB to extend your rage, you take 1d4 Psychic damage, and the rage extends for another round.

name: Ether Spear
descriptionMarkdown:
*Simple Weapon, very rare (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d6 force (or 1d8 force versatile) | **Properties:** Thrown, Versatile | **Weight:** 3 lb

---

This Spear can slip through the Ethereal Plane to reach its destination. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals Force damage instead of Piercing. When you take the Attack action while holding the Spear, you can choose a space you can see within 20 feet of you. The tip of the Spear vanishes and reappears in that space, allowing you to make melee attack rolls with the Spear against a target within 5 feet of that space until the end of the turn. These attacks ignore Cover|XPHB|Half Cover and treat Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover as if it were Cover|XPHB|Half Cover instead.

**Ethereal Sight.** You can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to magically see 60 feet into the Ethereal Plane while on the Material Plane and vice versa. This effect lasts for 1 minute. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Everice Box
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon*

**Weight:** 25 lb

---

This large wooden box weighs 25 pounds and is 3 feet long, 2 feet deep, and 2 feet tall. It has rugged ropes on its left and right sides as well as on the top of its lid. The left and right sides of the box are covered by enchanted slabs of stone that magically keep the contents on the inside of the box at a consistent 40 degrees Fahrenheit. The box can hold up to 24 Rations (or an equivalent amount of food). For a creature stuck inside the box to escape, it or a creature within 5 feet of the box must make a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check, freeing the trapped creature on a success.

While the box's lid is closed and its latch is shut, you can take a Magic action and use a command word to shrink it and its contents down to a more portable size. The weight of the box and anything inside it is halved while it's shrunk in this way, and the box measures a mere 1 foot long by 8 inches deep and tall. You can repeat the command word to return the box to its normal size. Opening the latch, whether by choice or by force, immediately returns the box and its contents to their full size and weight. A living creature can't be shrunk in this way, and the lid and latch are forced open if the box becomes too small for it.

name: Everlasting Sugarbomb
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, common*

---

This large sugarbomb is roughly two inches in diameter. Its flavors are a mix of bitter, salty, savory, spicy, sour, and sweet, but also refreshing. The sugarbomb is solid and slowly dissolves in your mouth, changing in flavor each time you reach a new layer. An Everlasting Sugarbomb provides enough nourishment to sustain a creature for one day after 1 minute of letting it dissolve in your mouth. The sugarbomb fully dissolves after 30 uses. You can bite through to the center of the sugarbomb with a successful DC 25 Strength or Constitution check (your choice). If you succeed, make a DC 16 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you have the Poisoned condition for 1 minute and suffer from painful nausea.

name: Eye of Dendallen
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, rare (Requires Attunement)*

---

While you're attuned to this item, you can cast the See Invisibility spell from it at will.

**Curse.** The Eye of Dendallen is cursed. When you attune to it, you must make a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw as you're suddenly overcome with the urge to see what it sees. On a successful save, you are aware of the curse's effects and can immediately end your attunement to the eye before it extends the curse to you. On a failed save or if you choose not to end your attunement to it, you are cursed until you are targeted by a Remove Curse spell or similar magic. When you become cursed, you forcefully tear out one of your own eyes, taking 4d10 Necrotic damage, and allow the Eye of Dendallen to crawl into the now vacant socket. If you're already missing an eye, you simply let the eye crawl into that socket without taking the Necrotic damage.

You can see normally through the Eye of Dendallen while it's in your socket. In addition, you have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet. If you already had Darkvision, the eye increases its range by 30 feet. As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can focus on looking through the eye to see through magical Darkness|XPHB for 1 minute as if it were nonmagical Darkness|XPHB. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

If your attunement to the eye ends after being cursed by it, it pulls itself out of your socket and tries to escape. The eye uses the Spider stat block except its creature type is Undead; it has HP 5; and it doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep. Slaying the eye while it isn't attuned to a creature destroys the item.

**Dendallen Familiar.** The eye also doubles as a gruesome companion while you're attuned to it. As a Magic action, you can command the eye to crawl out of your socket and move independently of you. You control the eye as if you summoned it with the Find Familiar spell, using the statistics above. If the eye drops to 0 Hit Points|XPHB or you dismiss it, it reappears inside your open socket with a sickly sound. If it does so as a result of dropping to 0 Hit Points|XPHB, it turns pitch black, and none of its magical properties can be used until the next dusk.

name: Eye of the Bookwurm
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon*

---

This small, glass sphere is enchanted with weak Divination magics to help you find specific words or phrases in writing. It has a stylized iris etched into the glass.

You can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to use a command word and then speak the word or phrase you're searching for. The word or phrase magically appears and floats within the sphere. By holding the eye in a free hand, your vision becomes magically enhanced to subconsciously highlight the word or phrase you searched for in a green light wherever you see it. Once you've used the eye's ability for the first time, you can change the word or phrase as many times as you like for the next hour, after which the item can't be used again until the next dawn.

**Damage:** 1d6 bludgeoning | **Weight:** 4 lb

---

Whenever you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll made with Fable's End against a Large or smaller creature, the target must succeed on a DC 15 Charisma saving throw or be banished to a harmless demiplane. At the end of its next turn, the target reappears in the space it left or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied. If you make an attack roll against a Fey with this weapon, you score a Critical Hit|XPHB and force the save against being banished on a roll of 19 or 20; Fey creatures have Disadvantage|XPHB on this save. When a creature is banished in this way, the weapon's center emits a brilliant magenta flash of light.

name: Fanfare Arrow
descriptionMarkdown:
*Ammunition, common*

**Weight:** 0.05 lb | **Value:** 0.05 gp

---

A favorite among tricksters, this ammunition is intended to distract rather than wound. When you make a ranged attack roll using this ammunition and hit, the target takes no damage, and the ammunition vanishes and is destroyed on impact. In its place, an instantaneous noise of your choice erupts from the point of impact, such as the sound of books falling, a dropped coin, or the breaking of glass. You decide the noise and its volume when you fire the ammunition. The sound can be as quiet as a whisper or as loud as a scream. A creature that hears the sound can determine that it is an illusion (no action required) with a successful DC 10 Intelligence (Investigation) check.

You can take a Magic action to place the coins over the eyes of a Humanoid that is dead, willing, or has the Unconscious condition. When you do, the coins create an effect based on which side is facing up. You can remove one or both of them from the creature's eyes as a Magic action to end the effect early. If the coins aren't facing the same direction, they have no effect.

**Heads.** While the coins are heads up over the eyes of a creature that has the Unconscious condition, that creature is Stable|XPHB. If placed over the eyes of a conscious creature, it enters a physical and mental state indistinguishable from death for 1 hour or until the coins are removed, and it has Immunity|XPHB to Psychic damage for the duration. Once a living creature leaves this state, it can't enter it again for 24 hours.

**Tails.** While the coins are tails up over the eyes of a dead creature, that creature is under the effect of the Gentle Repose spell. Its body can't be detected through magical means, and the soul of the creature can't be contacted.

---

This festerwood Rapier's blade is inlaid with scrapings from the Lightspore, the radiant mushroom growing at the center of the Festerwood. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. In addition, attuned to the Rapier, you have Advantage|XPHB on ability checks made to find locations within the Festerwood, and you are immune to magical contagions. While holding the sword, it sheds Bright Light|XPHB in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional 10 feet.

You can take a Magic action to raise the blade overhead and use a command word. When you do, all other creatures within 30 feet of you are dusted with a sudden wave of magical spores. An ally affected by the spores is suddenly invigorated, allowing it to immediately take a Reaction|XPHB to either make one attack roll using a weapon or an Unarmed Strike|XPHB or move up to half its Speed|XPHB without provoking Opportunity Attack. An enemy affected by the spores must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or have the Incapacitated condition until the end of your next turn. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dusk.

The Rapier has 5 charges for the following properties. It regains 1d3 + 2 expended charges daily at dusk.

**Spells.** While holding the Rapier, you can expend 1 charge to cast one of the following spells (save DC 17, +9 attack bonus) from it: Charm Person (level 4 version), Compulsion, Confusion, Contagion, Faerie Fire, Locate Animals or Plants, or Moonbeam (level 4 version). In addition, you can cast the Dancing Lights cantrip while holding the Rapier.

**Spore Cleansing.** As a Magic action, you can touch a willing creature with the Rapier and expend 1 charge to remove 1 Spore Counter from that creature.

You can hold this flame and other small nonmagical ones (such as that from a Candle or Torch) as if they were tangible objects and can sculpt them like clay. Once sculpted, a flame retains its form for 1 minute before returning to normal. A nonmagical flame carried in this way burns for 1 hour before dying. If you drop or throw a nonmagical flame, it immediately burns out.

When you cast Produce Flame using the gloves, the spell has a duration of 1 hour, instead of 10 minutes. In addition, you can place the spell's conjured flame on the ground at your feet (no action required). The placed flame is harmless and burns out after 1 minute, ending the spell, unless you take a Magic action to pick it back up while within 5 feet of it. Until you pick up the flame, you can't hurl fire as described in the spell unless you cast it again.

In addition, when you take Fire damage while wearing these gloves, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to reduce the damage by 1d8 + 2, provided you have a free hand.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, very rare (Requires Attunement)*

---

This patchwork shirt is made of enchanted pieces of stitched-together flesh. The shirt has 6 charges and regains 1d4 + 2 expended charges daily at dusk. While wearing the shirt, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB and expend 1 charge to cast the False Life spell. In addition, while you're Bloodied|XPHB, you regain Hit Points|XPHB equal to 1d4 plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1) at the start of each of your turns. You don't regain Hit Points|XPHB in this way if you have the Unconscious condition or have taken Fire or Radiant damage since the start of your last turn.

**Curse.** When you put on this cursed shirt for the first time, make a DC 20 Strength saving throw as the fleshy fabric begins to bubble, hiss, and fuse to your skin. On a successful save, you are aware of the curse's effects and can immediately remove the shirt before it extends the curse to you.On a failed save, you become cursed, and the shirt attaches to your flesh; you can't remove the shirt unless you are targeted by a Remove Curse spell or similar magic. Any nonmagical clothing you were wearing under the shirt is destroyed, and magical objects worn beneath it rise to the surface as it seeps through them to attach to your skin.

As long as you remain cursed, you have the Undead creature type in addition to any other creature type you already have, and you have Vulnerability|XPHB to Radiant damage. When you remove the shirt after being cursed by it, you take 4d10 Necrotic damage as the shirt is peeled from your skin.

name: Forgemaster's Maul
descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, legendary (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 2d6 bludgeoning | **Properties:** Heavy, Two-Handed | **Weight:** 10 lb | **Value:** 10 gp

---

This monumental hammer requires a Strength of 17 or higher to wield. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

You can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to use the command words, "light the forge," and cause flames to magically curl up and heat the hammer's anvil head. These flames shed Bright Light|XPHB in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional 20 feet. While the hammer is lit, it deals an extra 1d8 Fire damage on a hit and ignores Resistance|XPHB to Fire damage. The flames last until you take a Bonus Action|XPHB to use the command word, "quench," or until you drop or stow the hammer.

**Smith's Blessing.** You can use the hammer to cast either the Creation (level 6 version) or Fabricate spell as a Magic action instead of its normal casting time. When you cast Creation in this way, you can use its conjured materials as raw materials for the Fabricate spell, although the materials still have a limited duration. Once the hammer has been used to cast a spell, it can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dawn.

In addition, you know the Mending cantrip while you're attuned to the hammer. When you cast it to repair metal, the break or tear can be up to 5 feet in any dimension instead of 1 foot. You have Advantage|XPHB on ability checks using Smith's Tools to craft or repair an object when you use the hammer's head as the anvil.

**Iron Raze.** The hammer deals an extra 2d8 Bludgeoning damage to Constructs and structures on a hit.

name: Fortune's Fivepence
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon (Requires Attunement)*

---

This electrum coin has a smiling human woman's face on one side (heads) and a scowling fiendish woman's face on the other (tails). While you're within 30 feet of the coin, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB and use a command word to magically summon it to either your hand or pocket. Despite its unique appearance, this coin can be spent like a normal Electrum Piece.

**Fate Flip.** This coin has 2 charges. You can attempt to regain expended charges once every 24 hours by flipping a coin. The Fortune's Fivepence regains all expended charges if the coin is heads or 0 if it's tails.

When the coin is on your person and your total for a D20 Test|XPHB is 10 or lower, you can expend 1 charge (no action required) to channel the coin's magic and forge your own luck. When you do, flip a coin. If it's heads, add 1d10 to the D20 Test|XPHB; if it's tails, subtract 1d10 instead. The coin loses this property if using it reduces the total of your D20 Test|XPHB to 0 or lower.

name: Fourarm Bracers
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, very rare (Requires Attunement)*

---

These bracers can summon another pair of spectral arms below your existing ones. These arms can be summoned as a Magic action and last for up to 1 minute before disappearing. While active, you can use the spectral arms to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial.

Each arm can carry up to 10 pounds. The arms stay attached to your torso at all times and can't be moved to other parts of your body, but they can be turned around to face the opposite direction.

In addition, the gems adorning the bracers can amplify the arms' strength for short bursts. The gems have 5 charges and regain 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can use a command word and expend 1 charge to magically empower the arms and immediately make two Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes with them. The arms use a Strength modifier of +3 and use your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus for their attack rolls. They use a damage die of 1d4 and deal Force damage on a hit.

Alternatively, you can expend 1 charge when you summon the arms to double the amount of weight they can carry and increase their duration to 5 minutes.

name: Galea of the Soulfire Phoenix
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, artifact (Requires Attunement)*

---

This magical helmet once belonged to the Soulfire Phoenix Fara, a paragon to the citizens of the Elemental Plane of Fire who led her people to victory during the Savrayan Wars. While some believe that her ferocity and heroism were a result of phoenix blood running through her veins, others claim that a hero will always rise from the ashes when the time is right.

A spark of this heroism resides within the helmet, imparting its passion and phoenix-like properties to you. While wearing the helmet, you have Resistance|XPHB to Fire damage, and while you're in combat, magical flames erupt from it. The fire is harmless and sheds Bright Light|XPHB in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional 20 feet. If you die while attuned to the helmet, it vanishes in a cloud of embers and smoke and reappears somewhere on the Elemental Plane of Fire.

**Fiery Spirit.** While wearing the helm, you have Advantage|XPHB on saving throws to avoid or end the Charmed and Frightened conditions, and if you roll a 19 or 20 on the d20 for a Death Saving Throw|XPHB, you regain 1 Hit Points|XPHB. These benefits also extend to your allies within the helmet's Bright Light|XPHB.

**Ignite.** While wearing the helmet, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to cast the Fire Shield spell (warm shield only) from it. When you do, you also sprout a pair of flaming wings that last for the duration of the spell and give you a Fly Speed|XPHB of 30 feet. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

**Call of the Phoenix.** This helm has 7 charges and regains 1d4 + 3 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the helmet, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 18, +5 spellcasting ability modifier) from it: Death Ward (3 charges), Flame Strike (4 charges), or Healing Word (level 2 version; 1 charge).

**From the Ashes.** If you are reduced to 0 Hit Points|XPHB but not killed outright while wearing the helmet, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to call upon the spark of heroism that resides within the galea to drop to 1 Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point instead. When you do, you immediately regain 14 Hit Points|XPHB, and each creature within 10 feet of you must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw, taking 4d10 Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. In addition, two flaming wings unfurl from your back, carrying you to an unoccupied space of your choice up to 60 feet away from you without provoking Opportunity Attack. The wings then disappear. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until 2 days have passed.

**Random Properties.** The Galea of the Soulfire Phoenix has the following random properties:

- 1 Artifact Properties; Major Beneficial Properties property
- 2 Artifact Properties; Minor Detrimental Properties properties
- 1 Artifact Properties; Major Detrimental Properties property

**Destroying the Helmet.** The only way to destroy the helmet is to feed it to an ancient phoenix. The phoenix dies and is immediately reborn as a result of the intense magic stored within the Artifact. When it's reborn, the phoenix has a pronounced crown of golden feathers upon its head. Regardless of how many times it's reborn, the phoenix retains this crown of feathers.

name: Galvanic Steelsnare
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, rare*

---

This magic Net is made with fine steel chains and has the H|XPHB|Heavy property. Magic, leaden weights line the edge of the Net and send shocking pulses throughout the metal. A creature can't make more than one attack during its turn while it has the Restrained condition from this Net.

While a creature within 30 feet of you has the Restrained condition from the Net, you can use a command word as a Bonus Action|XPHB to cause the Net to magically release a painful wave of electricity, causing the target to take 1d6 Lightning damage. If the target is made of metal or wearing metal armor, it takes 2d6 Lightning damage instead. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the start of your next turn.

To escape, the target or a creature within 5 feet of it must take an action to make a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check, freeing the Restrained creature on a success. A Small or smaller creature has Disadvantage|XPHB on this check. Destroying the Net (AC 12; 15 HP; Resistance|XPHB to Slashing damage; Immunity|XPHB to all other damage) also frees the target, ending the effect. Once destroyed, the Net magically repairs itself over the course of 1d6 + 1 days.

name: Gibberbox
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, rare*

**Weight:** 7 lb

---

This magic box is made of enamel and bits of bone that stick together with the gummy, red remains of a gibbering mouther. The box weighs 7 pounds and is 1 foot long and 6 inches wide and deep. You can open the box's wooden lid as a Magic action. When you do, the red paste inside the box swirls and forms a toothy mouth that starts incessantly babbling nonsense. A creature takes 1d6 Piercing damage if it touches the red paste and toothy mouth while the box is opened and babbling in this way.

Each creature that starts its turn within 20 feet of the open box and can hear the babbling must make a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature can't make Opportunity Attack until the start of its next turn and rolls a d8 to determine what it does during the current turn. On a 1-4, the creature does nothing. On a 5-6, the creature takes no action or Bonus Action|XPHB and uses all its movement to move in a random direction. On a 7-8, the creature makes a melee attack against a randomly determined creature within its reach or does nothing if it can't make such an attack.

This effect lasts for 1 minute or until the box's lid is closed again as a Magic action. Once this property is used, it can't be used again for 24 hours. Opening the lid again while this property is inactive results in a droning, gurgling sound that turns silent after 1 minute of the box being open. The paste is extremely elastic and can't be removed or separated from the box.

name: Grass Carpet
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, common*

**Weight:** 30 lb

---

This soft roll of turf is magically fertile. Its soil is 1 inch thick and allows plants of all kinds to grow well within it. Each roll of turf is 10 feet long and 5 feet wide. Its grass and soil are self-containing and will not grow beyond the size of the carpet. The carpet is so fertile that plants growing in its soil require only half the normal amount of sunlight and water they would normally need in order to grow.

For every 1 inch of the soil's depth, the carpet provides the same amount of nutrition as normal soil does with 1 foot, allowing plants whose roots are normally 1 foot in length to grow with only 1 inch of this soil. Folding the carpet over for added depth, or layering multiple Grass Carpets on top of one another, increases the soil depth to allow for larger plants to grow on the carpet.

The carpet weighs 30 pounds and takes 1 minute to roll up or out. While rolled up, it has a diameter of 1 foot. The carpet can be cut into smaller plots using a magical blade, with each plot measuring at least 1 foot long and wide.

---

This Dagger's blade is actually a large, enchanted blade of grass. As wind passes over the blade, it creates a soft, sweet note that magically begins to lull creatures to sleep. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The Dagger has 4 charges and regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using the Dagger, you can choose to forgo the attack's damage and expend 1 charge to attempt to put the creature to sleep. When you do, you swing the blade in a pattern around the creature that creates a magical lullaby. The target must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or have the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn, at which point it must repeat the save. If the target fails the second save, it has the Unconscious condition for 1 minute. This effect ends on a target if it takes damage or someone within 5 feet of it takes an action to shake it out of the effect. If the target succeeds on the second save, it takes 3d8 Psychic damage instead.

Creatures that don't sleep, such as elves, or that have Immunity|XPHB to the Exhaustion condition automatically succeed on saves against this spell.

name: Gravity Goblet
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, common*

---

This glass and silver goblet is enchanted with a harmless, strange magic. A liquid poured in the cup bends gravity in comical ways, often to the surprise and drenching of its drinker. When the cup is tilted, as if to drink, the liquid flows in the opposite direction of gravity, sliding up the cup instead of down it. Once the liquid reaches the edge of the cup, it immediately pours down as normal. Swirling the liquid causes it to flow in the opposite direction in which it's rotated. Any solid object other than ice that floats in the liquid is not affected by the cup's magic.

name: Grip of Dendallen
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, very rare (Requires Attunement)*

---

These black leather and bone chain gloves spread sickness and decay to anything they touch. While wearing the gloves, your Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes deal 1d6 Necrotic damage instead of the usual Bludgeoning damage. This damage is maximized if you hit a plant or Plant creature with the attack.

In addition, while wearing the gloves, you can cast one of the following spells (save DC 16, +8 attack bonus) from them: Blight, Contagion, or Vampiric Touch. This version of Blight has a range of Touch instead of its normal range. Once the gloves have been used to cast a spell, they can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dusk.

**Curse.** When you pull these cursed gloves over your hands for the first time, make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw. On a successful save, you are aware of the curse's effects and can immediately remove the gloves before they extend the curse to you. On a failed save, you become cursed, and the gloves' bone chains pierce your skin, latching onto the bone in your arms; you take 4d6 Piercing damage, and you can't remove the gloves unless you are targeted by a Remove Curse spell or similar magic.

While wearing the gloves, the flesh on your hands slowly rots. The stench can't be contained or masked through magical or nonmagical means. While your hands are rotting in this way, you have Disadvantage|XPHB on Charisma checks, and immediately after you regain all lost Hit Points|XPHB when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, you take 1d6 Necrotic damage. When you remove the gloves after being cursed by them, it takes 1d4 days for your rotting flesh to return to normal and its scent to fade.

You automatically fail any Dexterity saving throw you make while admiring yourself in the mirror in this way.

name: Hand of the Master
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon (Requires Attunement)*

---

This satin glove has no visible seams and can be easily flipped inside-out to wear on either a left or right hand. While attuned to the glove, you can fit it over a hand that is either missing fingers or missing entirely and have it function as a normal body part.

In addition, you can cast the Mage Hand cantrip at will using the glove. When you do, the spectral hand originates within the glove instead of at a point of your choosing. The glove covers the spectral hand as it carries out your commands, leaving your hand or limb uncovered while it does so. Casting Mage Hand in this way doubles both the duration of the spell and the amount of weight the hand can carry.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon*

---

This gaudy purple hat allows the wearer to perform some minor magical feats. The hat has 3 charges and regains 1 expended charge daily at dawn.

While holding the hat, you can expend 1 charge to cast the Find Familiar spell from it as a Magic action instead of its normal casting time, pulling the familiar from the hat. The summoned familiar must take the form of either a rabbit or dove, using the statistics of a Weasel or Owl, respectively. The familiar remains for up to 1 minute and can't be used to deliver spells.

In addition, while wearing the hat, you can cast the Prestidigitation cantrip from it, using only the "sensory effect" or "minor creation" (illusory image) options.

*Wondrous Item, common*

---

This vest is made from a luxurious, silky material that seems to always make the wearer appear more fit. The clothing gently hugs the wearer, redistributing weight and muscle to flatter and accentuate their physique. It seems to deflate sadly once taken off.

While worn, the fabric's color changes with the wearer's mood or flash of emotion. Refer to the table below for the vest's colors when affected by different emotions. While unworn, the fabric's color becomes a muted blue.

| Joy | Yellow |
| Love | Lime Green |
| Fear | Green |
| Sadness | Navy Blue |
| Disappointment | Indigo |
| Disgust | Violet |
| Jealousy | Black |
| Surprise | White |

descriptionMarkdown:

---

This magic Shield offers a degree of control over the seas. While holding this Shield, you have a +1 bonus to Armor Class|XPHB. This bonus is in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC. name: Immovable Button
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, common*

---

As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can press this iron shirt button against a piece of fabric and use the command word, "hold." When you do, the button magically attaches to the cloth, fixing itself in place even if it is defying gravity. The button must be attached to a piece of fabric that is either unworn or worn by a willing creature. It can hold up to 500 pounds of weight and magically prevents the cloth from tearing due to tension. More weight causes the button to deactivate and fall.

A creature can take a Utilize action to make a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check, moving the fixed button up to 10 feet on a successful check. If a creature takes a Study action to examine the button, the creature can determine that it is magical with a successful DC 10 Intelligence (Investigation) check, and if it's already activated, the creature knows that the fabric around the button can be cut away. The button remains fixed in place for 1 minute before falling. The button's magic is lost once it's been used in this way.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon*

---

This 10-foot-long rope smells of sulfur and crackles with embers when moved. As a Magic action, you can lay the rope down in a line next to you on solid ground and use a command word to set it ablaze. When you do, the rope becomes a 15-foot-tall wall of fire along its length. The flames are visible, but not opaque, and are 1 inch thick. Creatures other than you within 5 feet of the wall when the rope is ignited must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 2d4 Fire damage. A creature must also make this save when it enters the wall of fire for the first time on a turn or ends its turn inside the wall. The flames shed Bright Light|XPHB in a 15-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional 15 feet, and they vanish after 1 minute.

The rope rematerializes at the base of the flames when they vanish. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn. The rope can only be broken by magical means and becomes a nonmagical Rope once broken.
