name: Ionbreaker, the Tempest's Reach
descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, artifact (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d8 piercing | **Properties:** Ammunition, Heavy, Two-Handed | **Weight:** 2 lb

---

This bow was crafted by a powerful djinni in the Stormheart: a perpetual maelstrom of wind and electricity in the Elemental Plane of Air. Lost to time, it has remained in the storm for untold centuries absorbing the volatile magic that runs rampant there. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

**A Storm Is Coming.** Whenever you roll Initiative|XPHB while the bow is on your person, you can roll 1d10 and add the number rolled to the total.

**Fast as Lightning.** When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make one attack with the bow as a Bonus Action|XPHB.

**Discharge.** Immediately after you hit a creature with a ranged attack using the bow on your turn, the target and other creatures within 5 feet of it each take 1d8 Lightning damage. Once a creature takes Lighting damage from this property, it can't take this damage again until the start of your next turn.

**Chained Conduits.** When you hit a target with a ranged attack using the bow, that target becomes a conduit for electricity for 1 minute. You can use a command word as a Bonus Action|XPHB to cause all such conduits within 60 feet of you to magically electrify. When you do, 5-foot-wide Lines of electricity arc between all electrified conduits that are within 30 feet of each other. Each conduit takes 2d8 Lightning damage, and all other creatures that are in at least one of the Lines must make a DC 18 Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d8 Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Once a conduit has been electrified in this way, it is no longer a conduit. Once a creature or object takes Lighting damage from this property, it can't take this damage again until the start of your next turn.

**Maelstrom Marksman.** Once on each of your turns when you miss a target with a ranged attack using the bow, you can reroll the attack roll, making the attack against a different target you can see within 30 feet of the first one. You have Disadvantage|XPHB on this attack roll.

**Zephyr Step.** While holding the bow, you have a Fly Speed|XPHB equal to your Speed|XPHB and can hover as long as you are within 20 feet of the ground.

**Embrace the Storm.** While you're attuned to the bow, you're subjected to the chaotic magic of the Stormheart whenever you take Lightning damage. When you do, roll 1d8, using the table below to determine the resulting effect.

| 1d8 | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | You have Vulnerability|XPHB to Lightning damage until the end of your next turn. |
| 2 | You are thrown 20 feet in a random direction and have the Prone condition. |
| 3 | You have the Deafened condition for 1 hour. |
| 4 | You can't take Reaction|XPHB|Reactions for 1 minute. |
| 5 | You cast Fog Cloud centered on a point within 5 feet of you. The spell doesn't require Concentration|XPHB and you can't end it early, instead lasting for 1d4 rounds. |
| 6 | Up to three random creatures within 10 feet of you take 1d8 Lightning damage. |
| 7 | Your Speed|XPHB is doubled until the end of your next turn. |
| 8 | You have Immunity|XPHB to Lightning damage until the end of your next turn. |

**Random Properties.** Ionbreaker, the Tempest's Reach has the following random properties:

- 1 Artifact Properties; Minor Beneficial Properties property
- 1 Artifact Properties; Major Beneficial Properties property
- 1 Artifact Properties; Minor Detrimental Properties property
- 1 Artifact Properties; Major Detrimental Properties property

**Destroying the Bow.** The bow can be destroyed if it's struck by lightning in the Stormheart at the same time as it's hit by a hammer made of pure adamantine against a similarly adamantine anvil by a creature attuned to the bow. When it's destroyed, each creature within 60 feet of the bow takes 10d10 Lightning damage and 10d10 Force damage. If a creature is reduced to 0 Hit Points|XPHB by this damage, it's immediately turned to ash and can only be revived by a Wish spell.

---

You can click the boots together and cast the Polymorph spell on yourself, transforming into a Riding Horse. descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, uncommon*

**Damage:** 1d4 slashing | **Properties:** Finesse, Reach | **Weight:** 3 lb

---

This Whip is made using the shrunken tentacle of a great sea creature. It still writhes slightly on its own. As a Magic action, you can use the Whip to force a Large or smaller creature you can see within 10 feet of you to make a DC 13 Strength or Dexterity saving throw (its choice).

On a failed save, the target has the Grappled condition and takes 1d4 + 2 Bludgeoning damage.

To escape, the target or a creature within 5 feet of it must take an action to make a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check, freeing the Grappled creature on a success. While Grappled, the creature takes 1d4 + 2 Bludgeoning damage at the end of each of its turns.

You can't use the Whip to attack while grappling a creature in this way. While holding the Whip, you can end the grapple at any time (no action required), and if you move more than 10 feet away from the Grappled creature, you drag it with you, but every foot of movement costs you 1 extra foot unless the creature is Tiny or two or more sizes smaller than you.

name: Lightning Pylons
descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, rare*

---

These 3-foot-long rods are made using a blend of magic and science and normally come in sets of three. The pylons are tipped with a fragment of a blue dragon's horn. A Lightning Pylon can extend electricity to any neighboring pylons to create an electrical barrier between them. Each pylon has an electrical charge. Once a charge has been lost, it takes 12 hours to recharge.

You can place a pylon upright in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you as a Magic action. If a pylon within 5 feet of you has an electrical charge, you can use a command word as a Bonus Action|XPHB to magically electrify it. When you do, the pylon is electrified for 1 minute, after which it loses its electrical charge. Any other pylon with an electrical charge placed within 20 feet of an electrified pylon also becomes electrified, creating a wall of lightning between them that is 10 feet tall and 1 foot thick. The wall is opaque and sheds Bright Light|XPHB in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional 10 feet. You can have up to six pylons connected in this way at a time. Electrified pylons are magically bound to the ground until they lose their charge.

When the wall appears, each creature within its area must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw; creatures made of metal or wearing metal armor have Disadvantage|XPHB on this save. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d8 Lightning damage, and its Speed|XPHB is reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much Lightning damage, and its Speed|XPHB is halved instead. A creature must also make this save when it enters the wall for the first time on a turn or ends its turn within 5 feet of the wall.

Each magic pylon has AC 15, HP 20, and Immunity|XPHB to Poison and Psychic damage. A creature that touches an electrified pylon or hits it with a metal Melee weapon takes 1d8 Lightning damage for each pylon connected to it, including itself. When a pylon is reduced to 0 Hit Points|XPHB, it falls over and loses its electrical charge, ending any connection it has to other pylons. A pylon reduced to 0 Hit Points|XPHB can't be used again until 2 days have passed, at which point it regains all its Hit Points|XPHB.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon*

---

This silver lock pick twists and reorients itself to more easily open locks. You gain a +3 bonus on Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks you make with it to pick a lock. name: Mask of Dendallen
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, very rare (Requires Attunement)*

---

This skull mask covers the top of your face and offers several benefits while worn. The mask has 5 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dusk. While wearing the mask, you can expend 1 charge to cast one of the following spells (save DC 16) from it: Bestow Curse, Fear, Speak with Dead, or Tongues. You have Advantage|XPHB on Constitution saving throws made to maintain Concentration|XPHB on a spell you cast in this way. In addition, you understand any written language that you see.

**Curse.** When you place this cursed mask over your face for the first time, make a DC 16 Intelligence saving throw. On a successful save, you are aware of the curse's effects and can immediately remove the mask before it extends the curse to you. On a failed save, you become cursed, and the skin surrounding the mask is riddled with blackened veins and sickly gray skin; you take 5d10 Psychic damage, and you can't remove the mask unless you are targeted by a Remove Curse spell or similar magic.

While wearing this mask, you can't smell or taste anything, and you automatically fail any Wisdom (Perception) check that relies on smell or taste. In addition, whenever you roll a 1 on D20 Test|XPHB, you take 1d10 Psychic damage. When you remove the mask after being cursed by it, it takes 1d4 days for the veins and skin on your face to return to normal.

Your voice also changes. Use the table below to determine the new voice.

| d6 | Change to Your Voice |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Your voice deepens and does not echo. |
| 2 | Your voice becomes raspy and you overly enunciate consonant sounds. |
| 3 | Your voice becomes quiet, almost a whisper, but can still be heard as if spoken at a normal volume. |
| 4 | Your voice becomes high-pitched, and your laugh maniacal. |
| 5 | You slur your words, as if your tongue is suddenly too large for your mouth, and your spit releases a faint hiss as it escapes your mouth. |
| 6 | Your voice becomes that of another ally's and changes each time you complete a Long Rest|XPHB. |

On a failed save, you become cursed, and the skin surrounding the mask is riddled with blackened veins and sickly gray skin; you take 5d10 Psychic damage, and you can't remove the mask unless you are targeted by a Remove Curse spell or similar magic.

While wearing this mask, you can't smell or taste anything, and you automatically fail any Wisdom (Perception) check that relies on smell or taste. In addition, whenever you roll a 1 on D20 Test|XPHB, you take 1d10 Psychic damage. When you remove the mask after being cursed by it, it takes 1d4 days for the veins and skin on your face to return to normal.

Your voice also changes. Use the table below to determine the new voice.

d6Change to Your Voice
1Your voice deepens and does not echo.
2Your voice becomes raspy and you overly enunciate consonant sounds.
3Your voice becomes quiet, almost a whisper, but can still be heard as if spoken at a normal volume.
4Your voice becomes high-pitched, and your laugh maniacal.
5You slur your words, as if your tongue is suddenly too large for your mouth, and your spit releases a faint hiss as it escapes your mouth.
6Your voice becomes that of another ally's and changes each time you complete a Long Rest|XPHB.

name: Mask of the Pact Bearer
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon (by a Warlock)*

---

This mask looks like a normal wooden mask while no one is attuned to it. When you attune to the mask, your patron's lingering presence over you magically reshapes it to represent the visage of your patron. While wearing this mask, you can cast one spell from the table of spells shown in your level 3 Warlock subclass feature without expending a spell slot. The spell must be of a level equal to or less than your Warlock spell slot level. A spell cast in this way is always cast at its lowest level, regardless of your normal Warlock spell slot level. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

---

This immaculate silver hammer is polished to a mirror finish. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The weapon has 7 charges and regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the hammer, you can expend 1 charge to cast the Mending cantrip from it, touching the hammer to the object. name: Mastery Gem
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, legendary*

---

This red gemstone seems to glint with some sort of liquid inside. The gem is immune to all damage. It contains magic absorbed from countless other sources that it uses to overpower the attunement requirements of certain magic items. While holding this gem against an item with an attunement requirement you don't meet, you can ignore that requirement and attune to the item anyway; the item can't be a Legendary item or Artifact. The gem fuses to the surface of the item and encases the area around it in a crystalline shell.

You can end your attunement to the item as normal, even if the item is cursed. Ending your attunement to a cursed item in this way breaks the curse's effects on you. When you end your attunement to an item the gem is fused to, it detaches from the item, allowing you to use it on another one and leaving behind the crystalline shell. When it detaches in this way, it removes the item's magic with it, causing the item to become nonmagical.

name: Memento of the Shapeless Axe
descriptionMarkdown:
*Melee Weapon, legendary (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d6 slashing (or 1d8 slashing versatile) | **Properties:** Versatile | **Weight:** 3 lb | **Value:** 0.50 gp

---

This weapon was forged using the preserved remains of an ancient mimic. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can use a command word to magically reshape it into any kind of Melee weapon with which you're proficient that doesn't have the H|XPHB|Heavy or R|XPHB|Reach property.

When you hit a creature with this weapon, you can attempt to grapple the target with it (no action required), channeling the weapon's natural pseudopod form. The target must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or have the Grappled condition. Until the grapple ends, you can't attack or grapple another creature with the weapon. Releasing the weapon ends the condition on the target.

**Pseuperpod.** As a Magic action, you can make a melee attack roll against a creature within 30 feet of you using the weapon. The weapon stretches toward the target as a pseudopod, ignoring Half and Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover, and deals 6d8 Bludgeoning damage on a hit. After the attack, the weapon retracts back into its previous form. If you attempt to grapple the target with the attack, the save DC for the Strength saving throw increases to 15. On a failed save, the target is pulled up to 15 feet closer to you before being released from the weapon's grasp. If the target failed the save by 5 or more, it is instead pulled up to 30 feet closer to you and remains Grappled. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until 12 hours have passed.

**Limb Replacement.** If you're missing an arm or forearm, you can graft the weapon to yourself in its place. If you do, the weapon changes and reforms to match the missing limb. You can add your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus to any Strength (Athletics) check you make using the limb; your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus is instead doubled for such checks if you already have proficiency in the Athletics skill. You can alter the limb's form to turn it into a weapon or revert it to match the missing limb as needed (no action required).

name: Merry Berry
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, common*

---

This small fruit is highly sought after by cooks and sweet-lovers everywhere, both for its flavor as well as its unique sensory-enhancing properties. Eating a Merry Berry raw yields a taste and texture like that of a rich shortbread—the perfect way to end a day of adventure or travel.

Cooking the berry, whether it be in a cuisine or simply roasted over a campfire, brings out more magical effects. When properly cooked, a creature that eats the fruit has Advantage|XPHB on Intelligence and Wisdom checks that rely on smell or taste for the next 24 hours, as well as on ability checks made using Cook's Utensils for the duration.

Overcooking the fruit not only cooks out the berry's benefits but also results in a soggy and overall bland dish.

name: Mirrorlight Edge
descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, rare (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d6 slashing | **Properties:** Finesse, Light | **Weight:** 3 lb

---

This roughly hewn crystal sword bends light in unexpected and dangerous ways. As a Magic action, you can use a command word to cause it to emit up to two ghostly projections of itself. The sword can have up to two of these projections at a time, which last until you dismiss them (no action required). When swung, the ghostly projections make the sword difficult to see. When you miss a target with an attack roll using the sword while it has at least one projection, you can dismiss one of its projections to reroll the d20, and you must use the new roll.

When you hit a target with this weapon while it has at least one projection, the ghostly projections become razor sharp. Targets hit by the sword take an extra 1d4 Slashing damage for each projection it has.

The sword sheds Dim Light|XPHB in a 10-foot radius while it has one projection or in a 20-foot radius while it has two. Sheathing the Scimitar contains the projections and their light without dismissing them.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Simple Weapon, very rare (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d6 piercing (or 1d8 piercing versatile) | **Properties:** Thrown, Versatile, Light | **Weight:** 3 lb

---

This crystalline Spear bends the light it generates in such a way that it becomes tangible. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which has the L|XPHB|Light property.

While you hold the Spear in one hand and have another hand free, you can use a command word as a Magic action to create a ghostly projection of the Spear in your free hand. The projection uses the same weapon statistics as the Spear. When you create a projection in this way, you can make one attack roll with either the Spear or the projection as part of that action. If you make a ranged attack roll with the projection, it disappears after it hits or misses the target. If you're still holding the crystalline Spear when this happens, it magically recreates the projection in your free hand again (no action required).

The projection lasts for 1 minute, until you dismiss it as a Bonus Action|XPHB, or until a creature other than you holds it. If you drop or stow the crystalline Spear, its projection disappears until you hold the Spear again. The Spear can only have one projection at a time. While it has a projection, both the Spear and its projection shed Bright Light|XPHB in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional 10 feet.

name: Mockingblade
descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, uncommon (by a Bard)*

**Damage:** 1d6 piercing | **Properties:** Finesse, Light | **Weight:** 2 lb

---

This magic sword helps you more effectively add insult to injury. You are proficient with the Mockingblade while you're attuned to it. The sword has 6 charges and regains 1d4 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a creature with this weapon on your turn, you can immediately take a Bonus Action|XPHB and expend 1 charge to cast the Vicious Mockery cantrip from it, using your spell save DC, against that creature. When you do, any words you use to insult the creature appear written along the blade for 1 minute or until replaced by a new insult.

When a creature rolls a 20 on its saving throw against a Vicious Mockery spell cast in this way, the face adorning the sword's hilt screams insults at you instead until the end of your turn. The insults are audible out to 30 feet and are directed at your deepest insecurities and regrets. Any creature that hears these insults is made aware of your weaknesses, granting it Advantage|XPHB on its next attack roll against you until the start of your next turn. Once the sword screams at you in this way, it can't be used to cast the Vicious Mockery spell again until 1d4 days have passed.

name: Monocle of Clarity
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, rare*

---

This single lens has three filters that you can peer through. You can change the monocle's filter by rotating its outer ring. A small arrow along the edge of the frame indicates the monocle's selected filter. The monocle has 4 charges and regains 1d3 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the monocle, you can expend 1 charge as a Magic action to activate one of the following filters and gain the corresponding benefits. These effects last for up to 1 hour, ending early if you take off the monocle or you change its filter.

**Filter of Comprehend Languages.** When you peer through this filter, you can understand any written language you see, as if by the written language portion of the Comprehend Languages spell.

**Filter of Darkvision.** While looking through this filter, you have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

**Filter of See Invisibility.** When gazing through this filter, you can see creatures and objects that have the Invisible condition as if they were visible.

descriptionMarkdown:

**Damage:** 1d4 slashing | **Properties:** Finesse, Reach | **Weight:** 3 lb

---

This mithral Whip was once used by a powerful monster hunter. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra 1d4 Slashing damage on a hit.

The Whip has seven runes on its handle that correspond to different damage types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, Radiant, or Thunder. When you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using the weapon, you can channel one or more of the runes to deal an extra 2d4 damage of the corresponding type or types. For example, you can channel two runes to add 2d4 Acid and 2d4 Fire damage to an attack against a troll, or one rune to add 2d4 Thunder damage to an attack against a clay golem. Once you channel a rune in this way, that rune can't be channeled again until the next dawn.

name: Null Chalk
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, very rare*

---

This drab pouch contains 1d4 + 1 sticks of dull gray chalk. The chalk feels slightly tingly to the touch.

As a Magic action, you can touch one of the sticks of chalk to the ground, wall, or ceiling to magically create a line that is up to 50 feet long and 1 foot thick. The line extends from your location in the direction and shape of your choice. You can shape the line in any way you choose as long as it makes one continuous path along the surface or similar adjacent surfaces. Once a stick of chalk has been used in this way, it disintegrates into a pile of fine, nonmagical powder.

Magical effects can't cross this line. The line's effect extends 20 feet perpendicularly from the surface on which it is drawn. Targets have Cover|XPHB|Total Cover against spells and other magical effects originating from the other side of the line. Magic items that cross the line become mundane and nonmagical for 1 round unless they're Artifacts.

The first time a Celestial, Elemental, Fey, Fiend, or Undead attempts to cross the line on a turn, that creature must make a DC 16 Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the creature's Speed|XPHB becomes 0 until the start of its next turn, it's forced backward up to 10 feet away from the line, and it takes 2d8 Force damage. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only, and it passes through the line. If the line cuts through an affected creature's space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the line (you choose which side).

This effect lasts for 8 hours or until a break of at least one foot is made in the line, which causes it to instantly lose all magical properties. A creature can spend 1 minute to smudge, smear, erase, or otherwise remove the line enough to disable its effects. When targeted by the Dispel Magic spell, the line is treated as if it were a level 6 spell. If the line is dispelled in this way, its effects are disabled for 1 minute.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon (Requires Attunement)*

---

This gruesome, magical otyugh pelt still holds some of its natural abilities. A single tendril bearing three eyes hangs from the back of the cloak's hood. While wearing the cloak, you can take a Magic action to telepathically communicate with a creature you can see within 60 feet of you that can understand a language, sending either simple messages or images when you do. The receiving creature can't respond to these messages.

The tendril hanging from the hood is 3 feet long and offers some limited articulation. While wearing the cloak, you can take a Magic action to mentally control the tendril enough to perform a simple task within 5 feet of you, such as to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial. The tendril can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

In addition, while wearing the hood, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to close your eyes and magically see through the eyes of the tendril. When you do, you have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet. You can control the tendril while looking through its eyes in this way. You return to your normal senses when you reopen your eyes or lower the hood.

name: Pack of LeviBubble Sugarbombs
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon*

---

This delicious gum comes in packs of five and can be blown into large, levitating bubbles 1 foot in diameter. You need to chew a piece of the gum for 1 minute before its magic can be used. Once it's been chewed for at least 1 minute, you can take a Magic action while the gum is in your mouth to blow a single bubble with it. When you do, you gain the effect of the Levitate spell, as if you had cast it, provided the bubble stays attached to the gum in your mouth. While the effect doesn't require your Concentration|XPHB, it does end early and cause you to fall if you take an action to pop it or if the bubble takes any damage; the bubble is a loose object for the purpose of any attack or effect that would target it. The effect ends on its own after 10 minutes, allowing you and the bubble to float gently down to the ground if you're still aloft. The gum becomes nonmagical, albeit still delicious, once this bubble's effect ends.

When you take the Magic action to blow this bubble, you can remove it from your mouth as part of the same action and stick it on another creature or loose object within 5 feet of you. When you do, the stuck target gains the effect of the Levitate spell, instead of you, but you have no control over it; the effect otherwise functions as described above. An unwilling creature that succeeds on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw avoids having the bubble stuck to it.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, rare (Requires Attunement)*

---

This magic Quiver is made from the shell of an enormous oyster. Arrows you pull from it are magical and are coated with a pearlescent, hydrophobic coating. Ranged attack rolls made with these Arrows ignore the normal drawbacks of underwater combat. The Arrows become nonmagical once they hit a target or are held by a creature other than you.

**Create Pearl.** You can use a command word to cause the Quiver to create a magical pearl. You can hold onto this pearl or give it to another creature. When a creature with the pearl makes a Wisdom check or Wisdom saving throw, it can choose to make the check or save with Advantage|XPHB. When it does, the pearl turns to dust. The pearl is visibly magical and disintegrates on its own after 24 hours if left unused. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Pendant of the Tempered Fury
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, very rare (Requires Attunement)*

---

This magic silvered pendant glows with a simmering flame of rage trapped inside its clenched fist. Small sparks shoot out from between the pendant's metal fingers. The fiery anger from the pendant tightens your focus and allows you to shrug off some of the damage you take. If you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield while you wear this pendant, all Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage you take is reduced by 3.

In addition, the pendant has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. You can take a Bonus Action|XPHB and expend 1 charge to ignite your hands in a magical flame, causing them to shed Bright Light|XPHB in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional 10 feet. Whenever you deal damage with your Unarmed Strike|XPHB while your hands are wreathed in this fire, it can deal your choice of Fire damage or its normal damage type, and it deals an extra 1d4 Fire damage on a hit. Your hands remain lit for 1 minute or until you take a Bonus Action|XPHB to quench them.

Any flame created by the pendant, whether it be on your hands or on the pendant itself, is harmless to you.

name: Peppermince Sugarbomb
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon*

---

This hard, minty sugarbomb slowly dissolves in your mouth over the course of 1 hour. At any point, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to crunch down and break the sugarbomb into tiny, painful shards. You take 1d6 Piercing damage from the shards but are temporarily enchanted by the candy. Whenever you hit a target with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike|XPHB that deals Piercing or Slashing damage while you're enchanted in this way, the target takes an extra 2 damage. This enchantment fades after 1 minute.

**Upset Stomach.** You can only be under the effects of one sugarbomb that has this property at a time. Eating a sugarbomb that has this property while under the effects of another one causes the effects of the first sugarbomb to immediately end and be replaced by the new one's. This rapid change is difficult to stomach, forcing you to make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you have the Poisoned condition for 1 minute.

name: Periapt of Reflection
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, rare (Requires Attunement)*

---

This perfectly reflective charm magically helps you meditate and focus your mind. Whenever you fail an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw while wearing the necklace, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to reroll the save, and you must use the new roll.

**Curse.** This periapt is cursed, a fact that is only revealed when the curse extends to you due to rolling a 1 on a saving throw after using the periapt to reroll it. Until the curse ends, the mirrored surface of the necklace dulls into an ugly, flat gray while you wear it. The curse persists even if you aren't wearing the necklace, and you remain cursed until you are targeted by a Remove Curse spell or similar magic.

While you're cursed, your reflection in any mirrored surface within 10 feet of you turns into an ugly, horrifying visage of your deepest insecurities. In addition, when you fail an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw (including the roll that reveals this curse), you take 1d8 Psychic damage.

name: Permanent Parchment
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, common*

---

This violet piece of parchment is smooth and pleasant to write on. You can take a Bonus Action|XPHB and use either of the command words, "lock" or "unlock," to magically lock or unlock the parchment, respectively. While locked, the sheet can't be torn by hand, damaged by fire, or damaged by immersion in water, and any ink already on the page can't be removed, smeared, or otherwise changed without the use of magic. New ink added to a locked sheet of Permanent Parchment runs off the page like water. While unlocked, the parchment behaves like a nonmagical sheet of paper.

If the sheet is unlocked, you can use another command word, "clear," to cause any ink on the sheet of parchment to magically evaporate without leaving any marks behind.

---

This crystalline Battleaxe seems to be almost transparent when looking at the bladed head from different angles. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which has the T|XPHB|Thrown property with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet. The first time on your turn when you hit a target with a ranged attack roll using the axe, you can force another creature within 10 feet of the target to make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, that creature takes 1d8 Force damage.

If you can see the axe and are within 60 feet of it, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to magically return the axe to your outstretched hand. When you do, the weapon phases through any obstacle in its path that isn't more than 5 feet thick or made of lead.

name: Phoenix Arrow
descriptionMarkdown:
*Ammunition, rare*

**Weight:** 0.05 lb | **Value:** 0.05 gp

---

This Arrow or Bolt is fletched with phoenix feathers and is magically bound to a small Quiver or Crossbow Bolt Case, respectively. You have a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this piece of magic ammunition. Once fired, the ammunition bursts into flames upon impact, dealing Fire damage on a hit instead of Piercing. At the start of your next turn, the ammunition leaves behind a small pile of ash and reappears in its container.

You can use a command word as a Bonus Action|XPHB before firing the ammunition to magically set it ablaze. If you fire it on that same turn, the ammunition deals an extra 1d6 Fire damage on a hit and immediately turns to ash; it turns to ash before reaching its target if fired more than 30 feet away. The ammunition reappears in its container immediately after turning to ash.

You can store up to ten other Arrows or Bolts in the small Quiver or Crossbow Bolt Case, respectively, but can only have one piece of Phoenix Ammunition bound to it at a time. If the ammunition is ever destroyed, it reappears in its container after 24 hours unless it was destroyed while rendered nonmagical, such as by an Antimagic Field.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, legendary (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d10 piercing | **Properties:** Heavy, Reach, Two-Handed | **Weight:** 18 lb

---

You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The weapon has 6 charges and regains 1d4 + 2 expended charges daily at dusk. While holding this Pike, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 17) from it: Mirror Image (1 charge), Phantom Steed (1 charge), Speak with Dead (1 charge), or Spirit Guardians (2 charges).

**Spectral Warrior.** Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with this Pike, you can choose to summon a spectral warrior from it. Until the start of your next turn, the target is haunted by this warrior, causing it to have Disadvantage|XPHB on attack rolls against you. This property has no effect against Undead creatures.

**Haunting Phalanx.** You can take a Magic action while holding this Pike to expend 3 charges and point it forward commandingly. Five spectral, Pike-wielding warriors appear before you and march in a 25-foot-wide, 50-foot-long Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line in a direction you choose. Any creature within the area must make a DC 17 Intelligence saving throw; Undead creatures automatically succeed on the save. On a failed save, a target takes 3d10 Necrotic damage and 3d10 Psychic damage and is affected by the weapon's Spectral Warrior property. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only.

name: Plaguebane Mask
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, rare*

---

This birdlike mask's blend of magic and science is as unique as it is helpful. While wearing it, you can easily lift it above your face to eat or speak more clearly. The mask's beak is lined with magical flowers that react to and purify airborne toxins before they pass through it. While wearing the mask, you have Advantage|XPHB on saving throws to avoid or end the Poisoned condition as well as the effects of magical contagions if they came from an airborne source, and you have Resistance|XPHB to any Poison damage that those effects might deal.

In addition, the flowers have 3 charges and regain 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn as new flowers bloom. As a Magic action, you can hold the beak's nostrils closed with a free hand and expend 1 charge to exhale a 15-foot Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone of thick pollen in front of you. Each creature in the area must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 2d8 Poison damage, and its Speed|XPHB is halved until the end of its next turn unless it has Immunity|XPHB to the Poisoned condition. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only.

name: Planar Rapier
descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, very rare (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d8 piercing | **Properties:** Finesse | **Weight:** 2 lb

---

This thin blade seems to toe the line between planes of existence, occasionally allowing it to bend the planes to extend beyond its normal reach. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The Rapier has 5 charges and regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. When you make a melee attack roll with the Rapier, you can expend 1 charge to extend the weapon, increasing its reach for the attack by 5 feet.

Alternatively, you can expend 1 charge immediately after making a melee attack roll with the Rapier against a target within 5 feet of you, causing the weapon to extend and pierce through the original target. Make an additional melee attack roll with the Rapier against a second target 5 feet behind the original one; the second target must be within 10 feet of you. This additional attack is made as part of the initial attack, and the second target doesn't benefit from using the original one as cover.

Whenever you expend a charge from this weapon, the planes around the extended blade begin to tear, causing the target to take an extra 2d8 Force damage on a hit.

After the attack with the extended blade, it returns to its normal size.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, common*

---

This canister of waxy pomade has magical properties, allowing you to change your hair's color, style, thickness, and length (up to 1 foot longer or shorter per use). The canister steadily replenishes its pomade over time. It can hold up to 4 uses at a time and regains 1d4 expended uses daily at dawn. Applying 1 use of the pomade takes 1 minute.

Once you've used this product in your hair, it returns to its normal appearance after you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. Hair produced by the pomade that's been cut off turns to dust after 24 hours. If you use the pomade every day for 7 days to make the same changes, the changes become permanent.

name: Potion of Dragon's Breath
descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, varies*

---

Drinking this potion grants you a brief surge of draconic power. Once within the next minute, you can replace one of your attacks when you take the Attack action with an exhalation of magical energy, which has the same effects as the Dragonborn's Breath Weapon trait. The damage type for the exhalation is randomly determined from the Draconic Ancestors table in the Dragonborn species description when this potion is created. The amount of damage the exhalation deals and its save DC are determined by the potion's rarity, as shown in the table below.

| Rarity | Damage | Save DC |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Potion of Dragon's Breath (Uncommon) | 2d10 | 13 |
| Potion of Dragon's Breath (Rare) | 3d10 | 15 |
| Potion of Dragon's Breath (Very Rare) | 4d10 | 16 |

When crafting a Potion of Dragon's Breath, you can use the harvested stomach and gizzard of a fallen dragon in place of the raw materials normally needed to craft a magic item. If you do, the exhalation's damage type is determined by the kind of dragon the materials were sourced from, and the potion's rarity is determined by the dragon's age category: Uncommon (young dragon), Rare (adult dragon), or Very Rare (ancient dragon). Once you start crafting a Potion of Dragon's Breath in this way, if you don't spend at least 2 hours working to craft it on a given day before finishing it, roll 1d20. On a 1, the harvested materials are destroyed, and the potion spoils.

name: Precipit, the Formless
descriptionMarkdown:
*Simple Weapon, artifact (Requires Attunement)*

**Armor Class:** 3 | **Damage:** 1d6 bludgeoning (or 1d8 bludgeoning versatile) | **Properties:** Versatile | **Weight:** 4 lb

---

This magic coral staff was first found within the Great Reef of the Elemental Plane of Water. Its origins beyond that are entirely unknown, with some suggesting it was made by the plane itself rather than forged or crafted by a mere creature's hands. Attuning to the staff bestows some of its planar powers to you, allowing you to breathe underwater and ignore any of the drawbacks caused by a deep, underwater environment. In addition, while holding the staff, you have Resistance|XPHB to Cold damage.

This staff has 15 charges, which are used to power its various properties. The staff regains 1d8 + 7 expended charges daily at dawn.

**State Change.** The staff has a powerful control over the various states of water. As a Bonus Action|XPHB while holding the staff, you can mentally command the staff's ever-present bounty of water to magically change its state into a gas, liquid, or solid. The properties of each state are detailed below. Alternatively, you can expend 1 charge as a Reaction|XPHB when you are targeted by an attack or spell to force the staff to change its state more rapidly.

When you do, the staff's change is immediate, potentially affecting the outcome of the incoming attack or spell. You take this Reaction|XPHB when you know you are the target of the attack or spell, but before knowing the result of the roll.

**Gas.** When the staff enters its gaseous state, the water surrounding it becomes a fine mist. While holding the staff in this state, you gain the following benefits:

- You have Resistance|XPHB to Bludgeoning and Piercing damage.
- Your Speed|XPHB increases by 10 feet.
- You have a Fly Speed|XPHB equal to your Speed|XPHB.
- You can move through the space of any creature, regardless of its size, and another creature's space isn't difficult terrain for you.
- Opportunity Attack against you are made with Disadvantage|XPHB.

**Gas Spells.** While holding the staff in its gas state, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 18) from it: Cloudkill (5 charges), Fog Cloud (1 charge), Gaseous Form (3 charges), Misty Step (2 charges), or Wind Walk (6 charges).

**Tailwind.** While holding the staff in its gas state, you can expend 2 charges and use a command word as a Magic action to grant additional benefits to you and nearby allies. Until the end of your next turn, you and your allies within 30 feet of you can take the Dash action as a Bonus Action|XPHB and don't provoke Opportunity Attack by moving.

**Liquid.** When the staff enters its liquid state, the water surrounding the staff becomes a swirling torrent. While holding the staff in this state, you gain the following benefits:

- You have Resistance|XPHB to Bludgeoning and Slashing damage.
- Your Speed|XPHB increases by 10 feet.
- You have a Swim Speed|XPHB equal to your Speed|XPHB.
- You can stand on and move across any liquid surface as if it were solid ground.
- When an enemy that you can see misses you with a melee attack roll, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to force that creature to repeat the same attack against a different creature of your choice (other than itself).

**Liquid Spells.** While holding the staff in its liquid state, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 18) from it: Blur (2 charges), Control Water (4 charges), Create or Destroy Water (1 charge), Mirror Image (2 charges), or Water Breathing (3 charges).

**Tide Turner.** While holding the staff in its liquid state, you can expend 3 charges and use a command word as a Magic action to send out a wave of ethereal water to buffet and push your enemies. Each enemy of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must make a DC 18 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 4d8 Bludgeoning damage and is pushed either 20 feet toward you or away from you (your choice). On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only.

**Solid.** When the staff enters its solid state, the water surrounding the staff becomes a frozen shell. While holding the staff in this state, you gain the following benefits:

- You have Resistance|XPHB to Piercing and Slashing damage.
- Your Speed|XPHB is reduced to 5 feet.
- You have a +3 bonus to Armor Class|XPHB.
- If you're pushed against your will, the distance you are pushed is halved.
- You gain 10 Temporary Hit Points|XPHB at the start of each of your turns, which vanish if the staff changes state.

**Solid Spells.** While holding the staff in its solid state, you can expend some charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 18; +10 attack bonus) from it: Cone of Cold (5 charges), Ice Storm (4 charges), Ray of Frost (0 charges, or 1 charge to cast at level 5), or Wall of Ice (6 charges).

**Deep Freeze.** While holding the staff in its solid state, you can expend 4 charges and use a command word as a Magic action to send out a chilling blast to freeze your foes. Enemies of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 4d8 Cold damage, and its Speed|XPHB is reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a target takes half as much Cold damage, and its Speed|XPHB is halved until the end of its next turn instead.

**Random Properties.** Precipit, the Formless has the following random properties:

- 2 Artifact Properties; Minor Beneficial Properties properties
- 2 Artifact Properties; Minor Detrimental Properties properties

**Destroying the Staff.** The only way to destroy the staff is to keep it untouched by water for 100 years while on the Elemental Plane of Water, at which point it crumbles to dust. Any amount or precipitation (such as a puff of misty air, a drip of water, or the touch of ice) during that time reinvigorates the staff's bounty of water.

name: Prismatic Javelin
descriptionMarkdown:
*Simple Weapon, uncommon (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d6 piercing | **Properties:** Thrown | **Weight:** 2 lb

---

This dark crystal Javelin has a prismatic head that can refract light into beautiful displays of color. Immediately after you hit a target with a ranged attack roll using the Javelin, it disappears in a small burst of light before reappearing in your open hand.

As a Magic action, you can throw the Javelin at a point you can see within 120 feet of you and use a command word. The Javelin erupts at that point in a dazzling display of color and light, casting painful Bright Light|XPHB in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional 20 feet. Each creature of your choice within the Bright Light|XPHB that isn't behind Cover|XPHB|Total Cover must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. For each target, roll 1d6 to determine which beam of light affects it, consulting the table below. On a failed save, a target takes 2d10 damage of the type corresponding to the beam's color for each beam of light it is struck by. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

| 1d6 | Color | Damage Type |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | Red | Fire |
|  | Orange | Acid |
|  | Yellow | Lightning |
|  | Green | Poison |
|  | Blue | Cold |
|  | Special | The creature is struck by two beams of light. Roll twice, rerolling any 6. |

name: Profane Mask
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, common*

---

This cloth mask converts the words that pass through it into vile obscenities. While wearing the mask over your mouth, your words are heard as angry insults and swears instead of the ones you intend. You don't hear these words. If a creature takes a Study action to examine the words, the creature can determine that they aren't your own with a successful DC 10 Intelligence (Investigation) check. Verbal spell components, command words, and actual obscenities you say are unaffected by the mask's magic and are heard normally by creatures within earshot.

**Damage:** 1d4 piercing | **Properties:** Finesse, Light, Thrown | **Weight:** 1 lb

---

This chiseled wooden Dagger is a relic crafted from the bough of a holy tree and is always miraculously sharp. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra 1d4 Radiant damage on a hit. This extra damage increases to 2d4 when you hit an Undead with the Dagger, causing blue tongues of holy flame to flash along the weapon's edge.

When you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll made with this weapon against an Undead, you can choose to plunge the blade into the target's body and leave it there. When you do, the Dagger emits Bright Light|XPHB in a 15-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional 15 feet. The light is sunlight. While the blade is lodged in a target in this way, that target takes 3d4 Radiant damage at the start of each of its turns, and the Dagger continues to emit sunlight. To end this effect, the target or a creature within 5 feet of it must take an action to make a DC 16 Strength (Athletics) check, removing the Dagger on a success. Once removed, the blade vanishes and reappears on the ground at your feet or in your free hand (your choice each time).

This beautiful Spear has a long handle carved of ivory and is tipped with the spiraling horn of a unicorn. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

While attuned to the Spear, you have Immunity|XPHB to Poison damage and the Poisoned condition. In addition, you have Advantage|XPHB on Constitution and Wisdom saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

The Spear has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the Spear, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 17) from it: Calm Emotions (2 charges), Detect Evil and Good (1 charge), Dispel Evil and Good (5 charges), Greater Restoration (5 charges), Misty Step (2 charges), or Purify Food and Drink (1 charge). In addition, you can take a Magic action to expend 1 charge to touch a creature with the Spear. The target regains 2d8 + 2 Hit Points|XPHB, and the Poisoned condition ends on it if it had that condition.

**Charge.** If you move at least 20 feet in a straight line toward a target immediately before hitting it with a melee attack roll using the Spear, the target takes an extra 2d8 Piercing damage.

**Curse Breaker.** While attuned to the Spear, you are immune to being cursed by spells and other effects. If you are already affected by a curse when you attune to the Spear or are attuned to a cursed item, the effects of the curse are suppressed for you as long as you remain attuned to the Spear.

The Spear has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the Spear, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 17) from it: Calm Emotions (2 charges), Detect Evil and Good (1 charge), Dispel Evil and Good (5 charges), Greater Restoration (5 charges), Misty Step (2 charges), or Purify Food and Drink (1 charge). In addition, you can take a Magic action to expend 1 charge to touch a creature with the Spear. The target regains 2d8 + 2 Hit Points|XPHB, and the Poisoned condition ends on it if it had that condition.

Charge.

If you move at least 20 feet in a straight line toward a target immediately before hitting it with a melee attack roll using the Spear, the target takes an extra 2d8 Piercing damage.

Curse Breaker.

While attuned to the Spear, you are immune to being cursed by spells and other effects. If you are already affected by a curse when you attune to the Spear or are attuned to a cursed item, the effects of the curse are suppressed for you as long as you remain attuned to the Spear.

name: Purse Piglet
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, rare*

---

This ceramic piglet figurine is glazed with a friendly pink coating that's soft to the touch, and it has a hole in the top that can be stoppered with a cork. When you drop a coin in the piglet and stopper it, the figurine animates and imprints on you, considering you its owner. As the piglet's owner, you can magically learn how much money is inside it by holding and gently shaking it, causing it to oink happily.

Once animate, the piglet happily eats any coin handed to it, storing it inside. The piglet will spit out exact change when you or an ally asks for it, even converting the coins within it into larger or smaller denominations. The figurine can only hold coins and will spit or sneeze out anything else you place inside it. The piglet squeals with glee and prances about excitedly when you deposit or feed it coins. The piglet can eat up to 1,000 coins of any denomination every hour it spends eating them; it will eat Electrum Pieces with less enthusiasm. The piglet remains the same size regardless of how many coins are inside it.

The piglet is exceptionally loyal and will listen to commands given by you and allies you designate. It walks beside you or the nearest designated ally in their space as best it can, but it vanishes into a pocket dimension if neither you nor a designated ally is within 30 feet of it. The figurine can be magically summoned to you or a designated ally as a Bonus Action|XPHB by using the command words, "Come home, little piggy." You or a designated ally can tell the figurine to return to its pocket dimension by taking a Bonus Action|XPHB to use the command words, "Go to market, little piggy."

When asking for 10 percent or more of its total stockpile, the piglet looks disappointed before carrying out the request. The piglet can eject its own stopper and roll over on its back to empty itself of coins when it's asked for a large amount, but it will always retain at least one Copper Piece unless you physically remove it. The figurine returns to its inanimate form when there are no more coins inside it.

The piglet is a Tiny object and can be attacked while it is animate. It has AC 10, HP 5, Immunity|XPHB to Poison and Psychic damage, and Vulnerability|XPHB to Bludgeoning damage. If the piglet drops to 0 Hit Points|XPHB, it cries out and shatters into hundreds of ceramic pieces, causing the coins inside it to scatter. The piglet rematerializes before you again after 1d4 days. If you die, the piglet becomes distraught and empties itself of all its coins, returning to its inanimate ceramic form atop whatever coins were inside it.

Placing the piglet inside an extradimensional space created by a Bag of Holding, Portable Hole, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. When this happens, the piglet is permanently destroyed, and its contents are lost. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within 10 feet of the gate and not behind Cover|XPHB|Total Cover is sucked through it and deposited in a random location on the Astral Plane. The gate then closes. The gate is one-way and can't be reopened.

name: Puzzle Ring of Vitality, Life, and Power
descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, legendary (by a Paladin)*

---

This ring is blessed by a god of life and healing. While wearing the ring, you can use your Lay On Hands on a creature up to 10 feet away from you instead of needing to touch it.

**The Outer Ring.** The inner, golden ring is covered by a silver puzzle ring that grants various benefits. The puzzle ring is made up of three distinct bands. As the bands are fitted together in an elaborate and ever-changing puzzle, you radiate an aura that heals and supports you and your allies. As a Study action while holding or wearing the ring, you can attempt to solve one band of the puzzle, which must each be attempted within a set amount of time and in a fixed order:

- The first band slides into place with a successful DC 5 Intelligence (Investigation) check. Once solved, you begin to radiate an aura in a 30-foot Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation, which lasts for 1 minute. When you create the aura and at the start of each of your turns while it persists, you can restore 2d6 Hit Points|XPHB to one creature in it.
- The second band can then be solved with a successful DC 10 Intelligence (Investigation) check. When it slides into place, the aura's power increases. While in the aura, you and your allies have Resistance|XPHB to Necrotic damage, and your Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximums can't be reduced. If an ally with 0 Hit Points|XPHB starts its turn in the aura, that ally regains 1 Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point.
- After that, the third and final band can be solved with a successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check. When the band fits into place to complete the puzzle, the aura's power is maximized. While in the aura, you and your allies have Advantage|XPHB on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. When an affected creature makes a saving throw against a spell or magical effect that allows a save to take only half damage, it takes no damage if it succeeds on the save.

The aura ends early if you take off the ring or drop to 0 Hit Points|XPHB. Once the aura ends, this property can't be used again until 1 day has passed for each band that you solved. If you solve all three bands, roll 1d3 when the aura ends. On a 1 or 2, the number of days that must pass before this property can be used again is reduced by the number rolled. On a 3, this property can be used again immediately.

name: Quagmire Maul

**Damage:** 2d6 bludgeoning | **Properties:** Heavy, Two-Handed | **Weight:** 10 lb

---

This old, withered hammer seemingly belongs in a swamp. Regardless of the conditions the hammer is kept in, it is always damp and smells of bog water. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The hammer has 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. As a Magic action, you can expend 1 or more charges and slam the hammer into the ground at a point within 5 feet of you. The area in a 5-foot-radius circle centered on that point transforms into a sickly, swamp that lasts for 1 minute. This area is Difficult Terrain|XPHB. For each charge you expend after the first, the circle's radius increases by 5 feet. While you're holding the hammer, you can traverse the magical swamp as if it were normal terrain.

If you expend the last charge from the hammer, roll 1d20. On a 1, the hammer turns into viscous muck in your hands and is destroyed.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, rare*

**Damage:** 1d6 piercing | **Properties:** Ammunition, Light, Loading | **Weight:** 3 lb

---

This curious contraption is in fact a small, surreptitious Hand Crossbow that can be worn on a wrist or forearm without requiring a free hand to use it. In order to use the crossbow, you must also wear two special rings on adjacent fingers on the arm the weapon is attached to. One ring carries a thin but flexible string that connects to the firing mechanism of the crossbow. The other ring is equipped with a very small but functional blade that's used to sever the first ring's string. When the string is severed, the crossbow fires. It takes 1 minute to reload the crossbow and reset its rings.

While the rings are set and the crossbow is loaded, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to make a ranged attack roll with it. Alternatively, you can make this attack roll as a Reaction|XPHB at the start of your first turn of a combat.

---

This Shield has a hidden compartment inside it that can fire thick squid ink at attacking creatures. When a Large or smaller creature within 5 feet of you misses you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to press a button on the Shield's handle, spraying ink from the front of the Shield. name: Ring of Anchoring
descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, rare (Requires Attunement)*

---

While attuned to this hammered lead ring, you can breathe underwater, and whenever you're pushed, pulled, or otherwise moved against your will, the distance you're moved is reduced by 10 feet.

**Curse.** This ring is cursed. Attuning to it curses you until you are targeted by a Remove Curse spell or similar magic. The curse also ends if the finger that's wearing the ring is severed from your hand. As long as you remain cursed, you can't take off the ring, and the arm that's wearing it becomes unbearably heavy while you're underwater, giving you Disadvantage|XPHB on Strength and Dexterity checks until you resurface.

Whenever you become submerged in a liquid, you must make a DC 20 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, your arm becomes immobile for 1 minute; for the duration, you have a Speed|XPHB of 0, and you're dragged 30 feet downward at the start of each of your turns. On a successful save, you can move your arm, albeit sluggishly, for 1 minute; for the duration, your Speed|XPHB is halved, and you have Disadvantage|XPHB on attack rolls you make with the arm wearing the ring. If you're still underwater at the end of the minute, you must repeat the save. These effects immediately end once you're no longer submerged.

name: Seed of Rebirth
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, legendary (Requires Attunement)*

---

This fist-sized, magic seed can be attuned to by four or fewer creatures over the course of a Long Rest|XPHB. If each creature attuned to the seed participates in gently planting it in fertile soil, the seed immediately begins to flourish, growing into a majestic, flowering tree over the course of 7 days. At the end of that time, the tree is 60 feet tall and 5 feet in diameter at its base, and its canopy extends out in a 30-foot Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation around the tree. The tree has a number of large limbs equal to the number of creatures attuned to the seed. Once planted in this way, no other creatures can attune to the seed, and the attuned creatures' attunement doesn't end as a result of being more than 100 feet away from the seed for 24 hours or dying. A creature's attunement to the seed immediately ends if it commits a malicious affront to nature.

When a creature attuned to the seed is dead for at least 1 minute, its soul returns to the tree, and its body crumbles into a rich soil that recreates the "enrichment" effect of the Plant Growth spell, centered on the body. The soul returns to the tree regardless of the circumstance of the creature's death or how far away it was from the tree when it died (even if it was on another plane of existence). The returned soul is stored in a shelled nut that the tree grows at the time of the creature's death from the large limb associated with that creature.

After 1d6 + 1 days, the nut falls from the tree and breaks apart, revealing the creature in its new body, as if by the Reincarnate spell. Once a creature is reincarnated in this way, its attunement to the seed ends.

When a creature's attunement to the seed ends, the tree limb associated with that creature withers and dies. The tree is magical and can't be destroyed by nonmagical means. If the tree is destroyed, all creatures attuned to the seed are no longer attuned to it. Any creature attuned to the seed is magically alerted if the tree is being attacked, if it's destroyed, or if one of its large limbs dies. Once all of the tree's large limbs die, the tree splits apart and disintegrates, releasing another Seed of Rebirth to the astral winds that carry it to a new location on a different plane of existence.

This necklace can animate small nonliving objects and have them fulfill simple tasks for you. As a Magic action, you can drape or wrap the necklace around a Small or smaller nonmagical object that weighs less than 50 pounds and isn't attached to or carried by anything else. The adorned object springs to life, sprouting little arms and legs, and becomes a mindless creature under your control until you remove the necklace or it takes damage. The servant has an AC of 10 and a Speed|XPHB of 20 feet.

As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can mentally command the servant if it's within 60 feet of you. The servant can perform simple tasks that a Human servant could do, such as fetching things, cleaning, mending, folding clothes, lighting fires, serving food, and pouring wine. The servant can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds. Once you give it a command, the servant performs the task to the best of its ability until it completes the task, then waits for your next command. If you command the servant to perform a task that would put it in danger or move it more than 60 feet away from you, the servant does nothing.

The necklace can animate an object for up to 8 hours or until it takes damage. When the effect ends, the necklace can't be used again for another 1d8 hours.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, rare*

---

This pair of candles are magically linked, and they never seem to run out of wick. They can be used as normal candles, but magically won't light Paper or Parchment on fire.

If you light one of the candles while the other one isn't lit, the first candle begins to burn with a blue flame. By holding a piece of Paper or Parchment over the flame, any nonmagical ink on the page is burnt off, leaving the page unmarked. When you finish using the candle in this way, you can extinguish the flame as normal.

Once the blue flame is extinguished, the linked candle immediately comes alight with a regular orange flame, which smells of lavender and can't be extinguished by nonmagical means. By holding a blank piece of Paper or Parchment over the orange flame, the ink from the first page is magically burnt onto the new one over the course of 1 minute as the candle heats it. Once all the ink has been transcribed onto a new page in this way, the orange flame winks out.

This wicked Dagger can absorb the shadows cast by your foes. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you hit a Small or larger enemy with a melee attack roll using this Dagger, you can choose to absorb that creature's shadow as part of the attack.

The dark haze remains for up to 10 minutes. A creature hit by the shrouded Dagger takes an extra 1d6 Psychic damage from the attack; this extra damage increases to 2d6 if the target is the creature missing its shadow. The haze ends early immediately after you make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell, or if you take a Bonus Action|XPHB to end it. Once the haze ends, the shadow immediately returns to the creature from whom it was taken.

You can only have one shadow absorbed in this way at a time. Once the Dagger steals a creature's shadow, it can't steal that creature's shadow again until the next dusk.

**Curse.** This Dagger is cursed. Attuning to it curses you until you are targeted by a Remove Curse spell or similar magic. As long as you remain cursed, you have Vulnerability|XPHB to Radiant damage.

name: Signet Rings of Blindness, Deafness, and Silence
descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, rare*

---

Each of these three signets is decorated with the carving of a skull and a pair of skeletal hands that cover either its eyes (blindness), ears (deafness), or mouth (in an area of silence). Each ring has 1 charge, which it regains daily at dawn. If you are wearing the corresponding signet when you have the Blinded or Deafened condition or are in an area of magical silence, you can expend that ring's charge (no action required) to end that condition or speak a word or phrase (such as a spell's Verbal component) that can be heard through magical silence. Wearing the rings together as a set combines their collective charges, potentially allowing you to use one ring's property multiple times.

name: Signet Rings of the Fey Court
reqAttune: by an Elf or Fey Creature
descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, very rare (by an Elf or Fey Creature)*

---

This set of wooden rings once belonged to a powerful Fey who ruled over a domain on the Feywild. You must be wearing all four rings in order to attune to them and use their magic. While wearing the rings, you know the Druidcraft cantrip. In addition, you gain the Elf's Trance trait if you don't already have it.

Each ring has an associated season: autumn, spring, summer, or winter. The four rings each contain 2 charges and regain all expended charges when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. Once a ring has no remaining charges, the small landscape adorning the top of it withers until it regains its charges.

**Season's Resistance.** You can expend 1 of a particular ring's charges as a Reaction|XPHB when you take damage of the type corresponding to that ring: spring (Radiant), summer (Fire), autumn (Necrotic), or winter (Cold). When you do, you have Resistance|XPHB to that damage type until the start of your next turn, including against the triggering damage.

**Magic Resistance.** You can expend any 2 charges from the rings as a Reaction|XPHB when an enemy targets you with a spell or other magical effect. When you do, you have Advantage|XPHB on saving throws against spells and other magical effects until the start of your next turn, including against the triggering spell or effect. The 2 charges don't need to be from the same ring.

name: Singing Stein
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, common*

---

While this pewter stein holds at least a sip's worth of potable alcohol, the face adorning it comes alive to sing songs based on the kind of drink it contains (examples are shown in the table below). If there are multiple kinds of alcohol within the stein, it either alternates between song types or does its best to combine their various lyrics. The stein isn't sentient, but it does have a pleasant singing voice. If there are multiple Singing Steins in the same room, they can sing together in harmony if they have the same kind of drink within them.

If the drink inside the stein is poisoned, it sings songs slightly out of key, which can be discerned by a creature that takes a Search action to make a successful Wisdom (Perception) check. The DC for this check is determined by the GM.

| Example Drink | Type of Song |
| --- | --- |
| Wine | Ballad |
| Rum | Sea Shanty |
| Ale | Drinking song |

name: Spire Seed
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, legendary (Requires Attunement)*

---

This large tree seed is 1 foot long and is surrounded by a protective cone. If you're attuned to the seed and plant it and its cone in soil, it immediately takes root and begins to grow rapidly, becoming fully grown after 30 days. The stem of the seed's cone is vaguely key-shaped, and it breaks off in your hand when planted. While you're attuned to the seed, the stem magically remains on your person at all times.

Once planted, no other creature can attune to the seed. Your attunement to the seed doesn't end as a result of being more than 100 feet away from it for at least 24 hours, but rather only after being on a different plane of existence than it for at least 24 hours. It also doesn't end as a result of you dying, but rather only after you've been dead for more than 1 minute. If your attunement ends after the seed has begun to grow but before it becomes fully grown, the tree dies and the seed is destroyed.

Once fully grown, the spire tree is 300 feet tall and 40 feet in diameter at its base, which tapers gently inward toward the top of the tree. Its canopy extends out in a 30-foot Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation around the tree. Soil beneath the tree's canopy is exceptionally rich and fertile.

At the base of this magic tree is a door large enough for Medium creatures to enter. The door is guarded by a Dryad who is loyal to you and allies you designate. The dryad accepts the seed's stem as proof of ownership and uses it as a key to open the door. If your attunement to the seed ends before the dryad first opens the door, the stem disintegrates and the door can't be opened. Once opened, your attunement to the seed ends, and the tree belongs to you. You and your designated allies can freely enter and leave the tree.

Inside the tree are ten floors. You choose how to distribute the floors throughout the tree. A wooden spiral staircase climbs upward through the center of the tree and its floors. Each floor has ten small windows that can't be seen from outside the tree. In addition, the interior of the tree can't be targeted by Divination spells or perceived through magical scrying sensors, and it can't be entered using teleportation or interplanar travel.

The tree has AC 20; HP 500; Immunity|XPHB to Poison and Psychic damage as well as Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage except that which is dealt by siege equipment, magic items, spells, or other magical effects; and Resistance|XPHB to all other damage. The door has AC 15, HP 100, and Immunity|XPHB to Poison and Psychic damage. The tree regains 1d6 Hit Points|XPHB daily at dawn. If a part of the tree, such as the door, is destroyed, that part regrows after 7 days.

If the tree is attacked, it immediately creates a Treant at its base to defend it. The treant isn't under your control and acts in accordance with its normal disposition and alignment, doing its best to defend the tree. The treant disappears at dawn or when it drops to 0 Hit Points|XPHB. Once the tree creates a treant in this way, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

Neither the treant nor the dryad can move farther than 1 mile away from the tree. If the dryad drops to 0 Hit Points|XPHB, it vanishes, reappearing at the base of the tree at the next dawn. If you or one of your allies kills the dryad, it doesn't reappear, and the tree becomes nonmagical. The tree is still hollow inside with the floors you'd chosen, but its windows and all its magical properties are lost.

The tree creates another Spire Seed once every 100 years.

name: Spirit Pike
descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, rare (by a Cleric)*

**Damage:** 1d10 piercing | **Properties:** Heavy, Reach, Two-Handed | **Weight:** 18 lb

---

If you're not proficient with Pikes, you are nevertheless proficient with this weapon while you're attuned to it. When you cast the Spiritual Weapon spell while holding the Pike, you can cause it to dissolve into the air to make the spell's spectral weapon take the form of the Spirit Pike. On a hit, with the spectral weapon, the target takes Force damage equal to 1d10 plus your spellcasting ability modifier instead of the spell's normal damage. If you cast Spiritual Weapon using a higher-level spell slot, the spell's damage still increases by 1d8 for every slot level above 2.

Your hands are left free when you dissolve the Pike in this way. When the spell ends, the Pike reappears in your hand or on the ground at your feet if your hands are full.

In addition, the weapon has 4 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. When you hit a target with an attack roll using the Pike as either a physical or spectral weapon, you can expend 1 charge to deal an extra 1d8 Radiant damage to the target.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, very rare (Requires Attunement)*

**Armor Class:** 1 | **Damage:** 1d10 slashing | **Properties:** Heavy, Reach, Two-Handed | **Weight:** 6 lb

---

This Halberd's haft is made of rough, dark wood and is miraculously easy to heft. The bladed end of the Halberd looks like a hatchet that's been absorbed by the hewn wood. While holding the Halberd with two hands, you can use a command word as a Bonus Action|XPHB to magically split the weapon into its more basic components.

When you do, the Halberd deconstructs in your hands, leaving you with a Handaxe in one hand and Quarterstaff in the other. Both the Handaxe and Quarterstaff have the L|XPHB|Light property. You can combine the two weapons to reform the Halberd by repeating the command word as a Bonus Action|XPHB while you're holding both the Handaxe and the Quarterstaff.

You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. If the weapon is split into the Handaxe and Quarterstaff, the bonus is a +1 with each weapon instead.

**Halberd.** If you hit a creature with the Halberd and roll a 10 on the damage die, that creature's energy is sapped. Its Speed|XPHB is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn, and your Speed|XPHB increases by 10 feet for the same duration.

**Handaxe and Quarterstaff.** If you're wielding the Handaxe and Quarterstaff in different hands, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class|XPHB, and when you make an extra attack as a result of using these weapons' Light property, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of that attack if you aren't already adding it to the damage. The Quarterstaff deals Necrotic damage on a hit, and it deals maximum damage to plants and Plant creatures. Immediately after you make a ranged attack with the Handaxe, it flies back to your hand.

This staff's form changes with the seasons. It has 10 charges and can be wielded as a magic Quarterstaff that grants a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it. As long as the staff has at least 1 charge, your melee attacks with it deal an extra 1d8 damage on a hit. This extra damage's type is based on the staff's season: spring (Radiant), summer (Fire), autumn (Necrotic), or winter (Cold).

Over the course of 10 minutes, you can focus on the staff to change its form to a different season. It remains in this form for 8 hours before reverting to the current season again.

While holding the staff, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells from it, using your spell save DC and spell attack modifier. The spells you can cast from the staff in this way are determined by its season, as shown in the table below.

| Spring | Guiding Bolt (1 charge), Moonbeam (2 charges), Plant Growth (3 charges) |
| Summer | Burning Hands (1 charge), Spike Growth (2 charges), Fireball (3 charges) |
| Autumn | Inflict Wounds (1 charge), Pass Without Trace (2 charges), Vampiric Touch (3 charges) |
| Winter | Color Spray (1 charge), Darkvision (2 charges), Sleet Storm (3 charges) |

The staff regains 1d6 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the staff loses all foliage and vitality, becoming a gnarled, nonmagical Quarterstaff.

descriptionMarkdown:
