---

This magic Spear is made of dark, polished granite and has a large ruby set in its head. Though it is made of stone, it weighs no more than a normal Spear and is enchanted to prevent it from shattering. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The Spear has 4 charges and regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn. While you're within 5 feet of a surface made of unworked stone or earth, you can take a Magic action and expend 1 charge to plunge the Spear into that surface. The Spear vanishes into the stone or earth and emerges as a sharp stone spike, 1 foot wide and 10 feet long, from another stone or earthen surface that you can see within 60 feet of you, such as the ground or a cave wall. The spike erupts perpendicularly from that surface and forces any creature in a 5-foot-wide, 10-foot-long Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line in that direction to make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 4d6 Piercing damage and is pushed up to 5 feet away from the spike. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

While you're within 60 feet of the stone spike and within 5 feet of a surface made of unworked stone or earth, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB and use a command word to magically recall the Spear. The stone spike crumbles, and the Spear inside vanishes back into the surface it erupted from before reemerging from the surface next to you into your open hand. If you don't have an open hand, it falls to the ground at your feet.

name: Starmetal Solar Axe
descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, legendary (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d12 slashing | **Properties:** Heavy, Two-Handed | **Weight:** 7 lb

---

This magic weapon is forged using iron from the stars. While you're attuned to this weapon, you can call upon its latent stellar energy to catalyze change within the metal, creating endothermic and exothermic reactions. The weapon can be fissioned into two separated Battleaxes or fused back into a Greataxe. It has the following properties based on its current state.

**Fused State (Greataxe).** You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra 2d6 Fire damage on a hit. While holding the axe, flames erupt from its edges and a small star burns in its center. These flames shed Bright Light|XPHB in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional 20 feet. The light is sunlight.

**Fissioned State (Battleaxes).** You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with each of these magic weapons, which deal an extra 1d6 Cold damage on a hit. The axes orbit you slowly while they aren't being held or stowed. You can equip an orbiting Battleaxe as if it were sheathed. In addition, if you take the Attack action on your turn, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to make one melee attack with an orbiting Battleaxe against a target you can see within 20 feet of you.

**State Change.** This weapon can change between its two states using the following properties:

**Fission.** While holding the fused Greataxe, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB and use a command word to magically split it apart into its fissioned state. When you do, electrical energy is released, forcing other creatures within 30 feet of you to make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 3d6 Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. This property can't be used again for 12 hours.

**Fusion.** While holding both fissioned Battleaxes, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB and use another command word to magically recombine the weapon into its fused state. When you do, the sudden generation of heat creates a wave of fire around you, forcing other creatures within 30 feet of you to make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 3d6 Fire damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. This property can't be used again for 12 hours.

descriptionMarkdown:

---

This gelatinous Net is made with the enchanted remains of a gray ooze. A creature takes 1d6 Acid damage when it gains the Restrained condition from the Net, and it takes that damage again at the end of each of its turns until that condition ends. If the creature is wearing nonmagical metal armor, its armor is partly corroded and takes a cumulative -1 penalty to the AC it offers whenever it takes Acid damage at the end of one of its turns. The armor is destroyed if the penalty reduces its AC to 10. The penalty can be removed by casting the Mending spell on the armor. A creature other than you who touches the Net takes 1d6 Acid damage.

The Net's sticky composition makes it more difficult to escape from than a mundane one. To escape, the target or a creature within 5 feet of it must take an action to make a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check, freeing the Restrained creature on a success. Destroying the Net (AC 10; 5 HP; Immunity|XPHB to Bludgeoning, Poison, and Psychic damage; Resistance|XPHB to all other damage) also frees the target, ending the effect and tearing the Net apart.

The torn Net is harmless. If more than half of the Net can be salvaged and stored within a container large enough to hold 5 gallons of liquid for 12 hours, the Net is repaired and can be used once more. Your attunement to the Net ends if the Net remains torn for longer than 48 hours.

You have Immunity|XPHB to damage from the Net while you're attuned to it. Picking up the Net after throwing it renders it harmless until the next time you throw it. The Net deals no Acid damage if there isn't a creature attuned to it.

**Damage:** 1d8 slashing (or 1d10 slashing versatile) | **Properties:** Versatile | **Weight:** 3 lb

This sword seems to absorb any light that touches it, making it appear darker than the deepest midnight. You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While holding the sword, you treat any magical light or Darkness|XPHB within 30 feet of you as if it were nonmagical, and you can breathe normally in any environment.

In addition, this sword has 2 charges and regains 1d2 expended charges daily at dusk. While holding the sword, you can expend 1 charge to cast Counterspell from it. When cast in this way, the target automatically fails its saving throw if the triggering spell is level 5 or lower, and it automatically succeeds if the spell is level 6 or higher. If you successfully interrupt a spell in this way, you can choose to absorb it into the sword instead of allowing it to dissipate. The absorbed spell must have a casting time of an action or a Bonus Action|XPHB. The sword can have only one absorbed spell at a time.

While holding the sword, you can release its absorbed spell. Doing so requires you to take a Magic action or Bonus Action|XPHB (as determined by the spell's normal casting time), and it uses the slot level, spell save DC, spell attack bonus, and spellcasting ability of the original caster but is otherwise treated as if you cast the spell.

The interrupted spell remains absorbed by the sword for 8 hours or until it's released. Absorbing a new spell replaces the one stored within the sword.

name: Tectonic Gauntlets
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, artifact (Requires Attunement)*

---

This magical set of stone gauntlets imbues your fists with the power of the Elemental Plane of Earth. While wearing the gauntlets, your Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes with your fists deal 1d8 Bludgeoning damage instead of the usual Bludgeoning damage (unless it's already higher), and they deal double damage to objects and structures. In addition, these gauntlets have 15 charges and regain 1d10 + 5 expended charges daily at dawn. When you make an Unarmed Strike|XPHB using your fists, you can expend up to 5 charges to extend your fist's reach by 5 feet for each expended charge.

**Powerglove.** When you hit a target with an Unarmed Strike|XPHB, you can expend up to 3 charges to deal an extra 1d8 Bludgeoning damage for each charge spent. If you spend any charges in this way, the target must also succeed on a DC 18 Strength saving throw or be pushed 5 feet away from you.

**Geomancy.** You can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 18) from them: Earthquake (8 charges), Move Earth (6 charges), Shatter (2 charges), Spike Growth (2 charges, with stone projections), or Wall of Stone (5 charges).

**Tectonic Plate Armor.** As a Magic action, you can cause rocks to envelop and protect your body. For 1 hour, you have Resistance|XPHB to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage, your Speed|XPHB is halved, and you have Disadvantage|XPHB on Dexterity checks and Dexterity saving throws. You can end this property early as a Bonus Action|XPHB. While enveloped in this way, you can burrow through nonmagical, unworked earth and stone using a Burrow Speed|XPHB of 30 feet. While doing so, you don't disturb the material you move through. If you end this property while burrowed in this way, you're shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take 1d10 Force damage. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until you finish a Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB.

**Curse.** These gauntlets are cursed. Your mind and body become sluggish once you attune to the gauntlets. The gauntlets become one with your flesh and prevent you from removing them. Your Speed|XPHB is reduced by 5 feet, and your Intelligence score is reduced by 4 (to a minimum of 7) while cursed. The curse remains even if the attunement ends but can be undone by any effect that removes a curse such as a Greater Restoration or Remove Curse spell, allowing you to remove the gauntlets and end the curse on you.

**Random Properties.** The gauntlets have the following random properties:

- 1 Artifact Properties; Minor Beneficial Properties property
- 1 Artifact Properties; Minor Detrimental Properties property

**Destroying the Gauntlets.** The gauntlets can only be destroyed in the depths of the crystalline mines of Durhun on the Elemental Plane of Earth where they were first created.

name: Tethervine Quiver
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon*

---

This seemingly overgrown Quiver keeps a large plant magically concealed inside it, and it can hold up to 20 Arrows or Bolts. When you draw an Arrow or Bolt from the Quiver, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB and use a command word to magically connect the end of the ammunition to the plant inside the Quiver. The plant is a ropelike vine that flies effortless behind its connected piece of ammunition when fired. It becomes taut and climbable if the ammunition hits an object or surface, able to hold up to 250 pounds before bursting.

While wearing the Quiver, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to magically retract the vine and its connected ammunition up to 60 feet back into the Quiver. If the connected ammunition hit an object that weighs less than 25 pounds, that object is also pulled back toward the Quiver when the vine is retracted in this way.

If you hit a creature with a piece of ammunition that was connected to the vine, the vine magically disconnects itself from the ammunition and falls. You can disconnect the vine from its connected ammunition by taking a Bonus Action|XPHB to repeat the command word or sever the vine from the Quiver.

The vine grows up to 120 feet long, and a connected piece of ammunition can't be fired longer than the vine's current length. If any portion of the vine is severed, it regrows up to 30 feet of length daily at dawn. A severed portion of vine becomes a mundane length of Rope.

name: The Griffon's Saddlebag
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, artifact*

**Weight:** 3 lb

---

These leather bags have the stylized face of a griffon on their front and appear across the multiverse in strange locations. One may be found in the belly of a dragon, while another in the limbs of a great tree. Regardless of where it's found, a Griffon's Saddlebag is typically discovered by an adventurer with a destiny.

The saddlebags are made by a great, six-armed griffon on the Astral Plane named Criir. Believed by some to be a demigod of pocket dimensions and craftsmen everywhere, Criir is a patron of artificers and creators across the multiverse.

The griffon creates magic items in its great forge using materials collected from various planes of existence to add to their collection. While no one knows exactly how to contact Criir, the astral griffon has a knack for knowing what items are needed by whom.

**Superior Holding.** This 1-foot-wide bag always weighs 3 pounds, regardless of what's inside it. It functions as a Bag of Holding that can only be pierced by another Artifact. Placing a Bag of Holding, Heward's Handy Haversack , Portable Hole, or similar item inside the extradimensional space created by the saddlebag, or vice versa, destroys the other extradimensional item but leaves the saddlebag unharmed. Any item stored within the other extradimensional space is magically moved to the space within the saddlebag instead. If doing so overloads the bag, random contents from either space are scattered in the Astral Plane until the bag isn't overloaded.

**Magic Courier.** At the GM's discretion, the saddlebag's beak opens up to reveal a letter. The magical script can be read by any creature with an Intelligence of 4 or higher. The note is a delivery request or similar task that includes the name of an item as well as either specific or vague descriptions of a person or place. At the bottom of the letter is a price listed in coins or other form of payment as well as a date or time depending on the task's urgency.

If the saddlebag is brought to the described person or place within the allotted time, it dispenses the magic item into the hand of the appropriate recipient. If the payment isn't received by the bag within 1 hour of dispensing the magic item, the item vanishes and is lost. After receiving the payment for an item in this way, the bag's beak reopens to dispense a reward for the courier.

**Sell Magic Items.** The saddlebag has a connection to Criir's forge on the Astral Plane. Depending on the magic item, you can sell a magic item to the saddlebag for half the cost of its base price.

**Spells.** The saddlebag has 8 charges and regains 1d6 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the saddlebag, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells from it: Detect Magic (1 charge), Identify (1 charge), or Legend Lore (5 charges).

**Additional Spells.** At the GM's discretion, such as after reaching certain milestones or completing Magic Courier quests, the saddlebag may offer one or more of the following additional spells that can be cast from it: Blink (3 charges), Dimension Door (4 charges), Divination (4 charges), Etherealness (7 charges), Fly (3 charges), Mordenkainen's Magnificent Mansion (7 charges), Plane Shift (7 charges), or Leomund's Secret Chest (4 charges).

**Sentience.** The saddlebag is a sentient Chaotic Neutral item with an Intelligence of 13, a Wisdom of 15, and a Charisma of 16. It has hearing and normal vision with a range of 60 feet.

The bag knows Common. When in the presence of only creatures it trusts, the bag can speak audibly, its beak moving as it speaks. Otherwise, the bag communicates telepathically with its wearer. The bag can also speak and communicate with griffons.

**Personality.** The bag's purpose is to carry, collect, and deliver magic items. Different bags have different personalities, but they are for the most part largely pleasant to talk to. Their voices are birdlike and are filled with occasional coos and squawks, and their stitched eyes widen, squint, and move expressively.

If the wearer or its allies fail to fulfill the bag's Magic Courier quests, it may stop offering its magic to them. If it does, their items may be lost or inaccessible within the bag or potentially spat out. While the bag provides the names of item recipients and delivery locations, it doesn't know any more information than what was provided to it by the astral griffon. Regardless, it does its best to help its wearer and allies find the specified person or location on the letter.

**Destroying the Griffon's Saddlebag.** While there is no way to permanently destroy the saddlebag, piercing it with an Artifact returns it to its place of origin for repair before it's returned to the multiverse in a new location. Placing a Griffon's Saddlebag inside the extradimensional space created by another Griffon's Saddlebag returns both items to their place of origin and sends all the items stored within them to Criir's forge on the Astral Plane.

name: The Rose Basket
descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, very rare (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d8 piercing | **Properties:** Finesse | **Weight:** 2 lb

---

This silver Rapier has a rose adorning its crossguard and pommel and has thorns lining its hilt. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. If you make an attack with the weapon against a Fey or a creature that is shape-shifted, the target takes an extra 1d8 Radiant damage on a hit.

**Field of Roses.** As a Magic action, you can use a command word and touch the Rapier's point to the ground at your feet. When you do, silver rosebushes sprout from the ground in a 25-foot square centered on your location. The area becomes Difficult Terrain|XPHB until the rosebushes disappear. When a creature moves into or within the area, it takes 2d4 Piercing damage for every 5 feet it travels. While holding the Rapier, this Difficult Terrain|XPHB doesn't cost you extra movement, and you don't take damage from moving into or within the area. The rosebushes disappear after 1 minute or when you dismiss them as a Bonus Action|XPHB. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Thornpiercer Dagger
descriptionMarkdown:
*Simple Weapon, legendary (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d4 piercing | **Properties:** Finesse, Light, Thrown | **Weight:** 1 lb | **Value:** 2 gp

---

This rose has a stem large enough to hold like the hilt of a weapon. As a Bonus Action|XPHB while holding it, you can cause the rose to magically grow one of the following weapons from its center: Dagger, Shortsword, Rapier, or Whip. If the hilt already has a weapon grown from its center, the existing weapon withers away and disintegrates, allowing the new one to take its place.

You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals an extra 1d4 Piercing damage on a hit. While attuned to Thornpiercer, you are proficient with the weapons it grows. Each weapon option has a unique property, as detailed below.

**Dagger.** When you throw this weapon, only the blade is thrown from the rose hilt. Hit or miss, the blade erupts into a burst of thorns after reaching its target. The target and up to three other creatures of your choice within 10 feet of it must succeed on a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw or take 1d4 + 2 Piercing damage.

**Rapier.** When you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll with this weapon, the blade's thorns eviscerate the inside of the target, dealing an extra 10 Piercing damage to it. If the target was a Large or smaller creature, it must also make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, its Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum is reduced by the amount of damage it took from the attack. On a successful save, its Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum is reduced by half that amount instead. This reduction to the target's Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum returns to normal when it finishes a Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB.

**Shortsword.** The first creature hit by this weapon on each of your turns must make a DC 17 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 1d6 Poison damage and has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn.

**Whip.** When you hit a Medium or smaller creature with this weapon, you can attempt to grapple it with the Whip. When you do, the target must succeed on a DC 17 Strength saving throw or have the Grappled condition. The Grappled target takes 1d4 Piercing damage from the Whip's thorns at the start of each of its turns until it's freed. To escape, the target or a creature within 5 feet of it must take an action to make a DC 17 Strength (Athletics) check, freeing the Grappled creature on a success. The Whip breaks off from the hilt when you successfully grapple a target in this way, allowing you to move freely while the target remains Grappled.

**Damage:** 1d8 bludgeoning | **Weight:** 2 lb

---

This Flail has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. As long as the Flail has at least 1 charge, you deal an extra 1d6 Lightning damage to the first target you hit with it on each of your turns.

While holding the weapon, you can expend 1 charge to cast the Thunderwave spell (save DC 15) from the ball of the Flail. Alternatively, if you make a melee attack using the Flail, you can immediately expend 1 charge to cast Thunderwave as a Bonus Action|XPHB in the direction of the attack's target.

The ball of the Flail is attached to its chain with a powerful magnetic connection that can be released at will. The Flail can be used to make special ranged attacks by releasing the ball mid-swing. You're proficient with these attacks, which have a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet, use your Strength modifier for their attack rolls and damage rolls, and deal 1d8 Bludgeoning damage on a hit. While the ball is within 60 feet of you, you can magically pull it up to 20 feet toward you as a Bonus Action|XPHB. It bounces harmlessly off of creatures and other objects in its path. The ball magically reattaches itself to the chain when it enters your space.

name: Timber
descriptionMarkdown:
*Simple Weapon, very rare (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d6 slashing | **Properties:** Light, Thrown | **Weight:** 2 lb

---

This magical axe is imbued with a destructive force that builds with each consecutive strike. You have a bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon equal to the number of charges it currently has. The Handaxe gains 1 charge each time you hit a target with it, up to a maximum of 3 charges. When Timber gains its third charge, the built-up energy immediately explodes; it loses all charges, and the target takes an extra 3d6 Force damage, or 6d6 Force damage if it's made of wood. When this happens, if the target is no more than one size larger than you, you can choose to push it up to 10 feet away from you.

Timber's charges last for up to 1 minute. It loses all charges if you miss with an attack using it, make an attack against a different target, or make an attack using a different weapon.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, very rare (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d8 piercing | **Properties:** Finesse | **Weight:** 2 lb

---

This item appears to be a sword hilt that has a small hole on either end of it. The hilt is made of clear quartz and contains an hourglass with sand inside it. Despite the holes on the hilt, the sand never seems to flow out of the hourglass. You can take a Bonus Action|XPHB and use a command word to cause it to magically form a thin blade of sand. The hourglass spills sand from the bottom of the hilt that circulates up and around to form the blade and guard of a Rapier before returning to the hourglass again through the hole at the top. You can take a Bonus Action|XPHB and repeat the command word to cause all the sand to return to the hourglass. While the Rapier is formed, you gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

While holding the hilt, you can cast either the Haste or Slow spell (save DC 16) from it. You have Advantage|XPHB on Constitution saving throws you make to maintain Concentration|XPHB on a spell cast in this way. While Concentration|XPHB|Concentrating on such a spell, the sands in the hourglass move quickly if you cast Haste or more slowly if you cast Slow. Once the hilt has been used to cast one of these spells, it can't be used to cast that spell again until the next dawn.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon (Requires Attunement)*

---

This small jade carving of a frog dangles from a simple cord of leather to be worn as a necklace. While you wear it, you gain a Swim Speed|XPHB equal to your Speed|XPHB and can hold your breath for up to 1 hour. In addition, you can cast the Jump spell using the necklace, targeting only yourself. Once the necklace has been used to cast this spell, it can't do so again until the next dusk.

**Curse.** This necklace is cursed. Attuning to it curses you until you're targeted by a Remove Curse spell or similar magic. Removing the necklace fails to end the curse on you. While you're cursed, your skin is perpetually slightly wet and clammy, and you have only an appetite for insects and other grubs instead of the foods you would normally enjoy eating.

name: Tome of Dreams
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon*

---

This beautifully embossed book is full of gripping short stories. You can read a story from the book in 10 minutes. The underlying nature of each story is unclear, leaving your subconscious mind to slowly process and unpack its deeper meanings over the course of your next Long Rest|XPHB.

The next time you finish a Long Rest|XPHB after reading a story from the book, roll 1d20. On a roll of 10 or lower, you take 2d4 Psychic damage as your mind is plagued with intense terrors from the story you read. On a roll of 11 or higher, you gain 2d4 Temporary Hit Points|XPHB as your mind is filled with joy and courage instead. If you start a story but don't finish reading it, nothing happens the next time you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

---

When held, a magical flame appears at the top of this weapon's handle. The flame sheds Bright Light|XPHB in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional 20 feet. You can snap the handle down as if cracking a whip (no action required) to cause the flame to extend into a 10-foot-long coil of fire, which you can use as a Whip. This weapon has the L|XPHB|Light property and deals Fire damage on a hit instead of Slashing. The flame doesn't hurt you while you hold the Whip. As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can snuff the fire out with your hand or blow it out to extinguish it.

The Whip's flame is intangible and can't be used to bind a creature or retrieve objects from afar, but can be used to light other fires.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Simple Weapon, rare*

**Damage:** 1d6 bludgeoning (or 1d8 bludgeoning versatile) | **Properties:** Versatile | **Weight:** 4 lb

---

A mote of swirling, magic water circles the top of this wooden staff, which can be wielded as a magic Quarterstaff. The staff can also be used to make special melee attacks by extending and lashing out with the water. You're proficient with these attacks, which have a reach of 10 feet, can use your Wisdom modifier for their attack rolls and damage rolls instead of Strength, and deal 1d4 Bludgeoning damage on a hit. After the attack, the water shrinks back to the staff. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, regardless of whether you attack with the weapon itself or use its special melee attack.

While holding the staff, you can stand on and move across any liquid surface as if it were solid ground. If you end your turn on a liquid in this way, you sink into it as normal until you stand on solid ground again. In addition, while holding the staff, you can cast the Control Water spell ("flood" or "part water" only) from it. The spell ends early if you are no longer holding the staff. Once the staff is used to cast this spell, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

name: Tote of Tricky Treat Sugarbombs
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, common*

---

This canvas bag holds 5d8 + 10 clove and pumpkin candies inside. A small illusory face appears over the sewn-on pumpkin at night. Each candy has a minor magical effect that lasts for 1 minute unless otherwise specified. Some effects are pleasant, whereas others are mischievous. You can eat a piece of candy as a Magic action. When you do, roll on the table below to determine the candy's effect.

| 1d20 | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | The candy seems to have spoiled, forcing you to succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or spend your action on your next turn retching and reeling. |
| 2 | Your face appears to melt, revealing the skull beneath it. The effect is harmless and illusory. |
| 3 | Any food you eat or water you drink taste like ash or blood, respectively. |
| 4 | Other creatures' eyes appear to be hollowed out and blackened to you. |
| 5 | Your ears turn a different, vibrant color at the start of each of your turns. |
| 6 | Your hair falls out and regrows over the next minute. |
| 7 | Your laughter becomes maniacal, and you have trouble stopping once you've started. |
| 8 | Your pupils resemble a snake's. |
| 9 | You hear a fly near your ear, but you can neither see it nor swat it away. |
| 10 | Your skin turns orange, and light spills forth from your eyes and mouth, shedding Bright Light|XPHB in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional 10 feet. |
| 11 | Confetti bursts from the top of your head, and small children can be heard laughing. |
| 12 | You sprout tiny, flightless bat wings. |
| 13 | You know the location of the nearest pumpkin within 1 mile. |
| 14 | Nearby crows and ravens land on your shoulders or outstretched arm. |
| 15 | A friendly, floppy wizard hat appears on your head. After 1 minute, it disappears in a cloud of stars. |
| 16 | Any alcohol in your stomach or that you drink becomes nonalcoholic. |
| 17 | Your voice becomes smooth and golden, allowing you to add your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus to Charisma (Performance) checks made to sing. If you already have proficiency in this skill, you have Expertise|XPHB in it instead. |
| 18 | Any food you eat or water you drink tastes delicious and reminds you of your favorite pastimes. |
| 19 | You gain Darkvision with a range of 30 feet. If you already have Darkvision, its range increases by 30 feet. |
| 20 | You can magically sense if a creature is possessed, and you can see creatures that have the Invisible condition. |

name: Trident of the Dryad
descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, uncommon (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 1d8 piercing (or 1d10 piercing versatile) | **Properties:** Thrown, Versatile | **Weight:** 4 lb

---

This magical wooden Trident has 4 charges and regains 1d3 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. While you're holding the Trident and are within 5 feet of a Large or bigger tree, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB and expend 1 charge to magically teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of a second Large or bigger tree that is within 60 feet of the previous tree.

**Tree Form.** You can take a Magic action to plant the bottom of this Trident in fertile ground and use a command word to transform it into a healthy tree. The tree is 60 feet tall and has a 5-foot-diameter trunk, and its canopy extends out in a 20-foot Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation around the tree. While you're within 5 feet of the tree, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB and expend 1 charge to magically teleport to another point on its trunk or within its branches.

The tree appears ordinary but radiates a faint aura of Transmutation magic that can be discerned with the Detect Magic spell. While touching the tree, you can take a Magic action and repeat the command word to return the Trident to its normal form. Any creature in the tree falls when the tree reverts to a Trident. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

name: Trident of the Hydra
descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, rare*

**Damage:** 1d8 piercing | **Properties:** Thrown | **Weight:** 4 lb

---

This oddly shaped Trident is made of hammered mithral and has a strangely short handle, but it is well-balanced for single-handed combat. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which lacks the V|XPHB|Versatile property.

When you make an attack by throwing the Trident, the forked end of the weapon magically splits apart to form three separate spears, allowing you to make three ranged attack rolls with it instead of one. These spears each deal 1d6 Piercing damage on a hit instead of the Trident's normal damage; you don't add your ability modifier to their damage unless that modifier is negative. After the attack, the Trident regrows its missing prongs from one of the separated spears, and the other two spears dissolve.

name: Tub of Churning and Fermentation
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, uncommon*

---

This squat, wooden and ceramic tub has a screw-on lid that fits snuggly around its base. The tub can hold up to 2 gallons of liquid or 1 cubic foot of material within it. You can leave a liquid or other perishable in the tub and secure the lid before saying the name of the end product you'd like the contents to turn into. If you say the name of a possible result, the tub clicks lightly before locking its lid shut.

After 10 minutes, the tub gives a second, louder click as the lid unlocks. The contents of the tub will have been stirred, processed, or otherwise fermented in such a way to generate the named end product. Adding extra ingredients into the tub can impact the end product's flavor.

Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

| Example Ingredient(s) | Potential End Product |
| --- | --- |
| Apples | Hard Cider |
| Assorted Fruits | Wine |
| Cabbage | Sauerkraut |
| Cucumbers and Vinegar | Pickles |
| Milk | Butter |
| Milk | Cheese |
| Milk | Yogurt |

name: Uorik the Conqueror's Juice Cup
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, common*

---

This brass cup changes the flavor of any water it's holding. As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can whisper the name of a fruit into the cup. If the cup is filled with water, the water's color and flavors magically change to resemble that kind of fruit juice. Saying the name of another fruit changes the water's color and flavors again. Regardless of its color and flavors, the water is still only water. Shouting into the cup causes the juice to effervesce and bubble. If the water is poisoned, the drink tastes foul and badly fermented.

name: Vancian Helm
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, rare (Requires Attunement)*

**Armor Class:** 1

---

This helmet is made from the reclaimed and partially disenchanted remains of a shield guardian, no longer bound to an amulet. You gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class|XPHB while you wear the helm.

**Spell Storing.** Any creature can cast a spell of level 1 through 4 into the helm by touching the helm as the spell is cast. The spell has no effect other than to be stored in the helm. The helm can only hold one spell at a time.

While wearing this helm, you can cast the spell stored in it. The spell uses the slot level, spell save DC, spell attack bonus, and spellcasting ability of the original caster but is otherwise treated as if you cast the spell. The stored spell is lost when it is cast from the helm or a new spell is stored.

If you are wearing the helm when a level 5+ spell is cast into it, the spell is lost with no effect, the spell slot used to cast it (if any) is expended, and you take 2d6 Psychic damage. Your eyes glow with a brilliant color of your choice when you wear the helm while a spell is stored within it.

While you're wearing the armor, you can't be caught in webs of any sort and can move through webs as if they were Difficult Terrain|XPHB. In addition, when you take Poison damage while wearing this armor, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to reduce the damage by an amount equal to 1d8 plus your Constitution modifier.

descriptionMarkdown:

**Damage:** 1d6 piercing | **Properties:** Ammunition, Light | **Weight:** 3 lb

---

This Hand Crossbow has a small spring-loaded case attached to its side, which can hold six Bolt and automatically loads the next Bolt into the crossbow whenever it's fired. While the case has Bolt in it, you ignore the crossbow's LD|XPHB|Loading property. A creature can take a Utilize action to reload the case with more Bolt.

The deployed crossbow is an object with AC 12, HP 30, and Immunity|XPHB to Poison and Psychic damage. If it's reduced to 0 Hit Points|XPHB, it falls over and can't be deployed again or used in this way for 1 minute. You can retrieve the deployed crossbow as a Bonus Action|XPHB while you're in its space.

name: Visage of Delight and Disaster
reqAttune: by a Creature with a Charisma of 17+
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, legendary (by a Creature with a Charisma of 17+)*

---

The expression of this mask subtly changes to reflect your expression and mouth's movement behind the mask. While wearing the mask, you gain two Bardic Inspiration dice, which are d10s (these dice are added to any Bardic Inspiration dice you have from another source). These dice are used in the same way and grant the same benefits as the level 1 Bard class feature, but they carry with them additional benefits based on the mood of your performance, as described below. You regain all expended Bardic Inspiration dice when you finish a Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB.

**Delight.** When you confer one of these Bardic Inspiration dice on a creature with a joyful or uplifting performance, that creature has Advantage|XPHB on saving throws to avoid or end the Frightened condition for 1 minute. In addition, when that creature uses the Bardic Inspiration die, it gains an amount of Temporary Hit Points|XPHB equal to twice the number rolled on the die.

**Disaster.** When you confer one of these Bardic Inspiration dice on a creature with a grim or haunting performance, that creature has Advantage|XPHB on saving throws to avoid or end the Charmed condition for 1 minute. In addition, when that creature hits a target with an attack roll using a weapon or an Unarmed Strike|XPHB, it can expend the Bardic Inspiration die, rolling the die and dealing extra Psychic damage to the target equal to twice the number rolled.

---

The boots have 10 charges and regain 1d6 + 4 expended charges daily at dawn. Choose an unoccupied space you just walked through for each expended charge. The ground and air in a 5-foot Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube within the chosen space or spaces become volcanic and impossibly hot for 1 minute. Any creature other than you that enters one of these Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cubes or starts its turn there must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 Fire damage. The Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cubes return to normal if you have the Unconscious condition or end the effect early as a Bonus Action|XPHB.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, rare (by a Spellcaster)*

---

These wands are sometimes found in the hands of clandestine mages posing as simple townsfolk. Its magic wax and iron design resembles a candle and candlestick. The wand produces a harmless, magical flame that is indistinguishable from normal candlelight, although the wax never melts or changes shape. The flame is harmless and sheds Bright Light|XPHB in a 5-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional 5 feet. While holding the wand, you can extinguish or relight the flame as a Bonus Action|XPHB.

This wand has 7 charges. While holding the wand, you can cast the Message cantrip from it, or you can expend 3 charges to cast the Sending spell from it. Alternatively, when you cast a level 0-5 spell while holding the wand, you can expend 1 charge per slot level to ignore the spell's Verbal components.

The wand regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dusk. If you expend the last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the magical flame burns out and the wand becomes a nonmagical Candle and candlestick.

---

While the standard is extended, you and your allies within 15 feet of it at the start of combat gain a +3 bonus to Initiative|XPHB.

This standard has 4 charges and regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn. If you're within 15 feet of the extended standard, you can expend 1 charge and shout the command word, "Charge!" to immediately take the Dash action as a Bonus Action|XPHB. When you do, your allies within 15 feet of the standard can take the Dash action as a Bonus Action|XPHB on their next turn.

You can change the emblem depicted on the standard over the course of 1 hour, which can be done during a Short Rest|XPHB.

descriptionMarkdown:
*Adventuring Gear, rare (by an Orc)*

---

This wand is made from the shattered hilt and jawbone of a defeated warband leader. It has 7 charges and regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll 1d20. On a 1, the wand releases a small gasp of breath as its magic escapes it, leaving the wand as a nonmagical sword hilt.

While holding the wand, you can use it to command and bolster your allies by expending 1 or more charges to use any of the following properties.

**Forced Endurance.** When an ally within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you is reduced to 0 Hit Points|XPHB but not killed outright, you can take a Reaction|XPHB and expend 2 charges to cause that creature to drop to 1 Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point instead. Once this property is used on a creature, that creature can't benefit from it again until it finishes a Long Rest|XPHB.

**Form Ranks.** You can expend 1 charge as a Magic action to maneuver one of your comrades into another position and bolster its resolve. When you do, choose an ally who can see or hear you. That ally gains 2d4 + 2 Temporary Hit Points|XPHB and can use their Reaction|XPHB to move up to half their Speed|XPHB without provoking Opportunity Attack.

**Unyielding Critical.** When an ally within 30 feet who can see or hear you scores a Critical Hit|XPHB, you can take a Reaction|XPHB and expend 1 charge to amplify the brutality of that attack. Roll 2d4 and add the total to the ally's damage roll.

**Warband Strike.** When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks and expend 1 charge to direct one of your companions to strike. When you do, choose a willing creature who can see or hear you. That creature can immediately use its Reaction|XPHB to make one attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike|XPHB.

---

While you're wearing the bag, creatures other than you have Disadvantage|XPHB on Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks to steal from the bag.

The bag and its eight straps adhere to the surface they're pressed against, such as your torso or the wall of a tavern. If you're wearing the bag, you can gently remove the straps from your body as a Magic action. Other creatures have Disadvantage|XPHB on Strength checks made to wrench the bag from you. The bag can hold up to 8 cubic feet or 80 pounds. Spiderskin is pliable and stretches easily, allowing the bag to shrink and grow to accommodate the objects placed inside to some degree.

While holding the weapon, you can expend 1 or more charge to cast one of the following spells (save DC 17, +5 spellcasting ability modifier) from it: Heroism (1 charge) or Wind Wall (3 charges).

Air Rend.

This weapon can manipulate the air around it to generate blades of wind, delivering devastating attacks at a distance. When you take the Attack action, you can replace one or more of your attacks, expending 1 charge for each attack you replace in this way. For each replaced attack, you make a special ranged attack against a target within 30 feet of you as if you were attacking it with the sword.

Sudden Storm.

When you take damage from a creature within 5 feet of you while holding the sword, you can take a Reaction|XPHB and expend 1 charge to make a melee attack with the sword against that creature. Additionally, if a creature hits you with a ranged attack roll, you can take a Reaction|XPHB and expend 1 charge to slash at the projectile and reduce the attack's total damage against you by 1d10 + 5. If you reduce the damage to 0, you destroy the projectile, provided it's nonmagical.

name: Wisplight Lantern
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, rare*

---

This dark Hooded Lantern doesn't require fuel; it continuously glows with a will-o'-wisp's blue flame that can reveal the final moments of a creature's life. As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can adjust the lantern's hood to change the light's radius, causing it to cast Bright Light|XPHB in a 5- to 20-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional number of feet equal to the chosen radius. Alternatively, you can close the lantern's hood entirely, causing it to cast no light.

The lantern has 4 charges and regains 1d3 + 1 expended charges daily at dusk. As a Magic action while holding the lantern, you can expend 1 charge and touch it to a Large or smaller corpse. When you do, a ghostly blue illusion of the fallen creature appears above its corpse and silently reenacts the last 6 seconds of its conscious life. The illusion only shows the creature's actions (for example, reacting to an unseen monster or trying to extinguish the flames of a fiery trap but not showing the responsible monster or effect). This property has no effect on Undead creatures. Once a corpse's death has been shown, it can't be shown by this Wisplight Lantern again.

Alternatively, while holding the lantern, you can take a Magic action and use a command word to expend 1 charge. If there are any Undead creatures within 60 feet of you that aren't behind Cover|XPHB|Total Cover, the lantern's light flashes red before returning to its normal blue glow.

name: Wyvernwing
descriptionMarkdown:
*Martial Weapon, rare (Requires Attunement)*

**Damage:** 2d6 slashing | **Properties:** Heavy, Two-Handed | **Weight:** 6 lb

---

This enchanted Greatsword contains a wyvern's wing that'sstretched between three thin, collapsed blades. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The sword has 4 charges and regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn. As a Magic action, you can expend 1 charge to flick open the sword like a fan and swing it down to create a buffeting wind. When you do, you can choose for the wind to either affect creatures in a 15-foot Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone or affect all other creatures within 5 feet of you. Each affected creature must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 2d6 Bludgeoning damage and is pushed up to 10 feet away from you. On a successful save, a creature takes half damage only. The weapon then magically collapses again as the wind settles.

name: Zafu of the Wandering Mind
descriptionMarkdown:
*Wondrous Item, rare (by a Monk)*

---

This soft, elaborately stitched pillow set focuses the intensity of your meditation. It takes 1 minute to settle into a meditation while sitting on the pillows. You can hold a light conversation while you meditate in this way but are otherwise unable to move or take actions. While meditating in this way, you can magically levitate yourself and the pillows up to 5 feet in the air. This meditation ends if you take damage, if you are no longer on the pillows, or if you decide to end it (no action required). While you're within 100 feet of at least one of the pillows, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB and use a command word to cause them to be magically shunted into a special pocket dimension. Repeating the command word as a Bonus Action|XPHB returns them softly to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.

In addition, this pillow set has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. While meditating on the pillows, you can expend 1 charge to cast the Arcane Eye spell without ending your meditation. If your meditation ends, your Concentration|XPHB on the spell is broken.
